minCreatedAt.description:
Minimum creation timestamp for filtering channels.

Filters channels created on or after this date. The ISO 8601 date-time format (e.g., '2024-01-15T14:30:00+09:00') is required for consistent parsing.

This parameter helps retrieve channels created within a specific time window for analytics, reporting, or audit purposes.

If not provided, the filter considers all channels regardless of creation date.

maxCreatedAt.description:
Maximum creation timestamp for filtering channels.

Filters channels created before or on this date. Like minCreatedAt, it uses ISO 8601 date-time format for proper timestamp handling.

When combined with minCreatedAt, this creates a date range for channel filtering, which is essential for time-based analytics and reporting.

This parameter is optional, but if provided, must be parsed correctly to maintain API reliability.

sortBy.description:
Name of the field to sort results by.

Determines the field by which channel data will be ordered. Common sort fields include 'name', 'createdAt', 'status', or 'type'.

The API validates that this value matches a supported sort field to prevent invalid sorting operations.

If not specified, the API defaults to sorting by 'createdAt' in descending order for the most recent channels.

oneOf.description:
Order direction for the sorting results.

'asc' for ascending order (A-Z, oldest-first), 'desc' for descending order (Z-A, newest-first). This parameter works in conjunction with sortBy.

When combined with sortBy, it determines the exact sorting behavior for channel listings.

If not specified, 'desc' is the default order to show the most recent channels first.

page.description:
Current page number for pagination. Must be a positive integer starting from 1. Used to calculate offset for database queries to support large result sets efficiently.

The minimum value of 1 ensures logical starting point for paging. Values below 1 would cause invalid pagination offset calculations and would be rejected by the system.

limit.description:
Number of products to return per page. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100 inclusive. This parameter helps balance between client-side data processing load and network efficiency.

The maximum value of 100 prevents overly large responses that could impact performance, especially on mobile devices. The minimum value of 1 ensures there's always at least one item per page.

search.description:
Full-text search query string. Used to search product names and product variant descriptions for matching results. Must contain at least one character to be valid.

The search function is designed to match partial words and handle common misspellings. It supports searching across multiple columns to improve user discoverability and provide comprehensive search results without requiring multiple separate search parameters.

category_id.description:
Filter products by category ID. When specified, only products belonging to the specified category will be returned. Should be a valid UUID string matching a category in the system.

This parameter enables category-specific browsing by allowing users to see all products within a specific category. Without this parameter, all categories are considered in the search results.

min_price.description:
Minimum price for products to include in results. When specified, products with price lower than this value will be excluded. Must be a non-negative number.

This parameter helps users narrow down products based on budget constraints. It's particularly useful for shopping experiences where price filtering is a common practice to improve user experience and result relevance.

max_price.description:
Maximum price for products to include in results. When specified, products with price higher than this value will be excluded. Must be a non-negative number.

This parameter works with min_price to create a price range filter, allowing users to find products within their desired price bracket. The combination with min_price creates flexible price range filtering.

oneOf.description:
Field to sort results by. Acceptable values are 'name', 'price', 'rating', or 'created_at'. Specifies the attribute by which product results will be ordered.

This parameter enables users to sort results by relevance (name), affordability (price), popularity (rating), or recency (creation date). The allowed values represent business-critical sorting options that align with common shopping patterns.

IShoppingMallProduct.IRequest.description:
Request DTO for product search operations, handling filtering, sorting and pagination across the product catalog.

This DTO provides an efficient interface for searching products with multiple dimensions of filtering including text search, category filtering, price range, and sorting options. It's designed for both customer and seller product search workflows, with appropriate security considerations in place to ensure privacy of inventory data.

The parameters are structured to support comprehensive search capabilities while optimizing for both performance and user experience. Fields marked as optional allow for flexible search specifications, with the required page and limit parameters ensuring all search requests include proper pagination.

IShoppingMallAdmin.IUpdate.description: Request DTO for updating an existing admin account with new details. This schema includes only editable fields, excluding system-generated identifiers and authentication context. Used for full-replacement updates where specified fields are replaced while preserving immutable system metadata. Designed as a partial object to support targeted field updates. Now includes all updatable fields from the database schema.

name.description: The name of the admin account used for internal identification and display in the administrative interface. This name appears in system logs, user management tables, and administrative interface panels. Should be a string of 1-255 characters with no special characters beyond spaces and hyphens.

email.description: The email address associated with the admin account used for notifications, password resets, and account verification. Must conform to RFC 5322 email standards and is treated as case-insensitive internally. Email addresses are stored in lowercase to ensure consistency across all system components.

oneOf.description: Contact phone number for the administrator used for emergency communications and verification purposes. Allows null for privacy preferences or when contact information is missing. Should be in E.164 format for international compatibility.
The phone number is not provided for the administrator, indicated by explicit null value instead of empty string.

phone.description: Contact phone number for the administrator used for emergency communications and verification purposes. Allows null for privacy preferences or when contact information is missing. Should be in E.164 format for international compatibility.

The system supports three predefined role types with strictly defined access levels. The database schema uses this field to implement role-based access control (RBAC) with fixed enum values.

The system supports three predefined role types with strictly defined access levels. The database schema uses this field to implement role-based access control (RBAC) with fixed enum values.

is_active.description: Current active status of the administrative account. This boolean value determines whether the account can be used for authentication and access to administrative features. Active accounts are usable, while inactive accounts require activation or deactivation. This field tracks whether the account is currently active in the system for authorization purposes.

IShoppingMallConfiguration.IRequest.description: Search parameters for filtering and pagination of configuration items. This DTO collects all parameters needed for efficient querying of configuration records with pagination and sorting capabilities. The page and size parameters are essential for standard pagination, while sort provides optional sorting criteria.

page.description:
Specifies the current page number for paginated results. The value must be a positive integer where 1 represents the first page.

This parameter is required to determine which segment of results to retrieve. Omitting this field would prevent correct pagination handling and is not allowed by the API protocol.

The page number must be greater than or equal to 1 to comply with standard pagination conventions across all platforms.

size.description:
Specifies the number of items to be returned per page. The value must be a positive integer and typically ranges from 10 to 100 based on platform conventions.

This parameter is required for pagination to define the segment size. Default values are not provided, so it must be explicitly specified on each call.

The size must be less than or equal to the maximum configured for the system (typically 100) to prevent excessive data retrieval.

sort.description:
Specifies the sorting criteria for results. Format should be 'field:direction' where field is the database column name and direction is either 'asc' or 'desc'.

Sorting parameters are optional, and when provided, will override the default order of results. The sorting field must correspond to a valid database column to prevent SQL injection or sorting errors.

Example values: 'name:asc', 'updated_at:desc'; unsupported sorting criteria will result in validation errors.

refresh_token.description:
Refresh token used to exchange for a new access token and extend the session.

This token must be valid in the customer_sessions table with at least 15 minutes of remaining validity to prevent immediate token reuse attacks.

The token is stored securely in the database and corresponds to the currently active customer session.

IShoppingMallCustomer.IRefresh.description:
Defines the request body structure for refreshing a customer's authentication session.

Contains the refresh token required to maintain session continuity without requiring re-authentication. The refresh token must be active and meet the minimum validity requirement of 15 minutes to prevent security vulnerabilities.

This schema supports the refresh operation while enforcing secure token rotation policies and session management standards.

IShoppingMallCustomerSession.description:
Customer authentication session object representing a specific valid authentication session for a customer account. This schema contains all necessary information to verify the current session state, including the token, expiration time, client IP address, and other metadata.

This session is used to maintain a secure connection between the client and server during the customer's login state, ensuring that subsequent API requests can be authenticated without requiring the customer to re-enter credentials. The session object is the core component for all customer authentication flows and security checks.

Session management follows strict security protocols, including automatic expiration after 1 hour of inactivity. The session data is stored in the shopping_mall_customer_sessions database table with encryption of sensitive fields. This schema ensures consistent session representation across all customer-facing API operations.

token.description:
Authentication session token used to validate the user's session. This token must be included in the Authorization header as Bearer token for subsequent requests.

This field is critical for session security and is generated during the initial authentication process. It is stored in the database and verified at each request to ensure session validity. The token is a unique alphanumeric string that expires according to the 'expiresAt' timestamp.

The token is generated following RFC 6750 standards for Bearer tokens and has a minimum length of 32 characters to prevent brute-force attacks. It is stored as a hash in the database, not as plain text, for security purposes.

expiresAt.description:
Timestamp representing when the authentication session will expire. This field is stored in ISO 8601 format and indicates the exact moment the session becomes invalid. After this date, the session token can no longer be used for authentication.

This value is determined during session creation and is based on the session's configured lifetime (typically 1 hour for customer sessions). It is used to enforce session expiration policies and security measures across the platform.

The expiration time is calculated using UTC time to prevent timezone-related issues. The system automatically refreshes active sessions before expiration to maintain uninterrupted user experience, but the exact expiration timestamp is calculated based on the original creation time.

clientIp.description:
IP address of the client device that initiated the authentication session. This value is used for security logging and monitoring purposes to identify the source of the login attempt. It is validated as a standard IPv4 address.

This field helps in detecting suspicious login attempts and enforcing location-based security policies. It is recorded at the time of session creation and serves as part of the session metadata.

The IP address is validated against RFC 791 specifications for IPv4 format and is stored in a normalized form (without any masking or redaction) for security audit purposes.

name.description:
Product name displayed in the shopping mall catalog.

Must be at least 1 character long and unique within the seller's product inventory.

Serves as primary product identifier for customers and SEO purposes.

Must be a meaningful name that reflects the product's purpose and value proposition.

description.description:
Detailed product description including materials, specifications, features, and benefits for customers.

Used for product pages, search results, and customer decision-making.

Should be comprehensive enough to inform customers about product value without being excessively technical.

price.description:
Product price in USD.

Must be positive and at least $0.01 to prevent free listings.

Strictly validated prior to creation to ensure all products have meaningful pricing.

Returned in the response with price as integer (cent amount) in business logic.

category_id.description:
UUID identifier for the category this product belongs to.

Must reference an existing category in the shopping_mall_product_categories table.

Used to organize products within the shopping mall's category structure and enables hierarchical navigation.

IShoppingMallProduct.ICreate.description: Product creation request with validation rules. Allows authenticated sellers to add products to their inventory with all required fields validated against the product schema. The system validates name uniqueness within seller's inventory, positive price, and valid category reference. Seller identity is provided automatically through JWT tokens.

IShoppingMallEmailVerificationToken.description:
Analytics data for email verification tokens including verification rates, success metrics, and token usage patterns. This type aggregates performance metrics from email verification operations to help administrators monitor system health and optimize verification workflows.

The analytics provide actionable insights into email verification success rates, token validity durations, and common failure patterns. These metrics directly correlate with data stored in the shopping_mall_email_verification_tokens table, which tracks all token-related activities including timestamps, email addresses, and verification status.

This DTO is designed for read-only access and must not include any personally identifiable information or sensitive token details. The data structure supports both summary views for dashboard displays and detailed breakdowns for deeper analytics investigations.

successRate.description:
Percentage of successful email verifications relative to verification attempts. Represents the rate at which email verification tokens were successfully processed and validated by the verification service.

This metric helps administrators identify overall system efficiency and potential issues in the verification flow. Successful verifications occur when the token matches the email address and remains valid within its configured expiration window. The value is calculated as a decimal between 0.0 and 1.0 (e.g., 0.85 for 85% success rate).

avgValidityDuration.description:
Average time tokens remain valid before expiration. Measured in ISO 8601 duration format (e.g., PT24H for 24 hours).

This metric provides insight into optimal token lifetime settings. The system calculates the average duration across all tokens before they expire or are verified, helping administrators determine if current expiration periods are suitable for user experience and security requirements. For example, an average of PT24H indicates most tokens are used within 24 hours of generation.

items.description:
Common patterns of failed verification attempts. Identifies frequent reasons verification fails including expired tokens, mismatched emails, and expired verification links.

This array contains string descriptions of common failure scenarios observed in the verification logs. Patterns include terms like 'token_expired', 'invalid_email', 'domain_blocked', and 'too_many_attempts'. Each pattern represents a specific issue category identified through the verification analytics.

failurePatterns.description: Detailed identification of common failure categories

totalVerificationAttempts.description:
Total number of verification attempts across all tokens generated in the measured period. Counts all attempts including successful and failed verification operations.

This metric represents the complete scale of email verification activity, making it essential for calculating success rates and understanding system usage patterns. The value increases with each token generation request regardless of verification outcome, providing context for the successRate metric.

verificationPeriodStart.description:
Start timestamp of the analytics data collection period. Defines the beginning of the timeframe covered by the metrics.

This field establishes the time boundary for the analytics, allowing administrators to correlate verification performance with specific system events or business periods. The value is formatted as ISO 8601 timestamp, representing the exact start time for calculating the metrics.

verificationPeriodEnd.description:
End timestamp of the analytics data collection period. Defines the conclusion of the timeframe covered by the metrics.

This complementary field to verificationPeriodStart establishes the complete timeframe for the analytics. It allows administrators to identify seasonal trends, system performance changes across intervals, and relate verification metrics to business events occurring within this window.

IShoppingMallCustomerSession.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a customer authentication session, designed for efficient display in session history lists. This type contains minimal but essential information required for customers to view and manage their active and historical authentication sessions without unnecessary data.

The summary format specifically excludes sensitive authentication tokens, expiration details, and other security-critical information that is retained in the backend for processing. Only user-observable session details are included, maintaining both security and privacy compliance. This schema is used in the response for the GET /shoppingMall/customer/customers/{customerId}/sessions endpoint, specifically in the IPageI<type>.ISummary format for optimized client-side data consumption.

The schema design aligns with the shopping_mall_customer_sessions database table to ensure accurate modeling of session data. Each summary item represents a record from the database but presents it in a condensed format suitable for list rendering. The implementation strictly follows the Atomic Operation Principle for Read DTOs, ensuring complete session information is available in a single API call for efficient frontend rendering.

session_id.description:
Display identifier for the session, shown to the customer in the session history list. This is a human-readable identifier that appears to the user as the unique session label, often with the date of creation and device type.

The format follows 'session-{YYMMDD}-{device}-{random}', and is designed to provide sufficient context to the user without revealing sensitive information. This field is the primary way a customer identifies their session history entries in the UI.

created_at.description:
Timestamp of when the session was created (when the customer logged in). This is formatted as ISO 8601 date-time string (e.g., '2023-08-15T14:30:00Z') and represents the exact time of session initialization.

This timestamp is displayed to the customer to help them remember when they last logged in from a particular device. The frontend uses this to order session history chronologically and to show the session creation time in the user interface.

last_activity_at.description:
Timestamp of the last activity within the session, indicating the most recent time the customer interacted with the platform while authenticated.

This timestamp appears in session history to help customers identify active sessions that are still in use. It's updated on every authenticated user action, providing real-time status to customers when checking their session details. The frontend uses this to identify sessions that are currently active versus those that have been idle.

device_info.description:
Summarized information about the device type and browser used for the session. This is a human-readable string that identifies the device to the customer, formatted as 'Device Type - Browser' (e.g., 'iPhone 14 - Safari').

This field provides customers with context about which devices they're logged into, helping them identify suspicious activity. The information comes from the device identifier stored in the database, but it's presented in a user-friendly format without technical details that could reveal security vulnerabilities.

location_info.description:
Summarized location information for the session, presented as a friendly human-readable string (e.g., 'Seoul, South Korea'). This is derived from the geolocation data stored along with the session record.

This information helps customers identify sessions that were created from unexpected locations. The location is presented in a simplified format to protect privacy while still providing useful context for session verification. It does not include latitude/longitude or other precise location data.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the seller session. Generated automatically upon successful authentication to reference specific session records within the system.

This field is used for session resource identification and is required for all session operations. The UUID format ensures globally unique session identifiers without collisions across the platform.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the session was first established. This is the moment of successful authentication when the session record was created.

The date-time format with UTC timezone ensures consistent timestamp handling across all platform components and international users. This timestamp is used for session lifetime calculations.

last_activity_at.description:
Timestamp indicating the most recent activity within this session. Updated whenever the session is used for any platform interaction.

This timestamp helps determine session validity and inactivity thresholds. The system uses it to invalidate sessions after extended periods without activity.

device_info.description:
Detailed information about the device used to initiate the session, including browser, operating system, and device type.

This data provides important context for security monitoring and fraud detection. It helps identify unusual login patterns and verify session legitimacy based on device characteristics.

ip_address.description:
IP address from which the session was registered. The IPv4 format ensures consistent handling of IP addresses across all platform operations.

This field is critical for location verification and security analysis. The system uses it to detect login attempts from unusual locations and may trigger additional security checks if the IP differs from the user's typical location.

seller.description:
Summary reference to the seller account that owns this session. Establishes the relationship between the session and the seller, ensuring sessions are linked to their authenticated owners.

This reference replaces the raw seller_id field per DTO transformation rules. The system validates that the seller reference matches the authenticated seller's identity before allowing any session access or modification, preventing unauthorized session viewing across seller accounts.

IShoppingMallSellerSession.description:
Represents a seller's authentication session with the platform. This schema provides detailed session information for authenticated sellers to view their current session status, connection metadata, and security context.

The response includes all non-sensitive session metadata while excluding security tokens per platform security protocols. This object is returned when a seller retrieves their own session details using the /shoppingMall/seller/sellers/{sellerId}/sessions/{sessionId endpoint.

Session details are crucial for security monitoring, access control, and platform analytics, providing insights into seller engagement patterns and security events.

IShoppingMallSellerSession.ISummary.description:
Session summary data for seller authentication tracking.

This type represents a concise snapshot of an active authentication session used by a seller to access the platform, designed for session management and security monitoring.

The schema excludes all sensitive token data while including essential session context such as creation and expiration times, device information, and geographical location. This ensures security compliance and minimizes data exposure in summary responses.

The fields accurately reflect the session's lifecycle and device context, which are crucial for identifying unauthorized login attempts and managing seller session status. All timestamps are stored in ISO 8601 format for consistency and ease of processing.

This summary type is used in the list response for seller sessions, where each session item provides the minimum necessary information for the seller to monitor their active sessions.

id.description: Unique identifier of the session used for session management and correlation.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the session was created, in ISO 8601 format.

expires_at.description: Timestamp when the session expires, in ISO 8601 format.

active.description: Indicates if the session is currently active (suitable for filtering active sessions).

ip.description: IP address of the device used to establish the session, for security monitoring and geolocation.

user_agent.description: User agent string from the original authentication request, indicating browser, OS, and device model.

location.description: Geographical location of the session origin, populated via IP geolocation for security context.

IShoppingMallAdminSession.description:
Detailed session information for admin authentication sessions, including authorization details, timestamps, device information, and expiration status. The session data is securely displayed, excluding the actual token value for enhanced security. Built as a main entity with full object relations for comprehensive session data view in admin contexts.

This schema provides all necessary information for secure session management without exposing sensitive credentials. It represents a single row from the shopping_mall_admin_sessions database table with all relevant session details, optimized for admin authentication workflows. The schema is specifically designed for the GET /shoppingMall/admin/admins/{adminId}/sessions/{sessionId} endpoint.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the admin session, assigned by the system upon session creation. This ID is the primary key in the session table and is used to reference the session in API operations like GET /shoppingMall/admin/admins/{adminId}/sessions/{sessionId}.

This UUID is generated using version 4 algorithm to ensure global uniqueness and security. The ID serves as the main identifier for session tracking, logging, and retrieval operations within the authentication system.

admin.description:
Reference to the admin account associated with this authentication session. Contains essential admin details including name, email, and role, but no sensitive credentials or authentication tokens. This is a belongs-to reference transformed from the database's admin_id foreign key.

This foreign key reference connects the session to the administrator's account record. The summary type provides all necessary account information without exposing sensitive authentication details or session tokens.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when the admin session was initially created. This value comes directly from the database's created_at column and represents the exact moment the session was established.

The timestamp is stored in ISO 8601 format for consistent date comparisons and sorting in the authentication management interface. This field serves as the starting point for tracking session duration and activity metrics.

expiresAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when the admin session will expire. If null, the session has an infinite expiration time (no expiration). This maps to the database's expires_at column, which can be null.

This nullable timestamp field follows database schema constraints for session expiration. When the value is null, the session remains valid indefinitely, which is typically reserved for administrative sessions requiring extended access. The database allows this column to be NULL to accommodate sessions with no expiration.

deviceInfo.description:
Details about the device and browser used to establish the session, such as 'Chrome 120 on iPhone 14 Pro'. This field is populated from the request metadata during session creation.

The device information provides critical security context for session validation and monitoring. It includes browser name, version, and device type to help identify suspicious activity patterns in the administrative account's session history.

ipAddress.description:
IP address associated with the session creation event. This field is derived from the client's network request and is stored as a string representation of the IPv4 or IPv6 address.

The IP address serves as an important security identifier for detecting unusual access patterns. It is stored as a standard string representation to allow for proper filtering and analysis within security monitoring systems.

content.description: Updated content for the review. Must be at least 1 character and no more than 1000 characters. The content should reflect the user's experience with the product.

rating.description: Updated star rating for the product review. Must be a whole number between 1 and 5 (inclusive). A value of 5 represents the highest rating.

IShoppingMallReview.IUpdate.description:
DTO for updating an existing product review. Allows updating the content and rating of a review without modifying other system-managed fields. Content must be 1-1000 characters, rating must be 1-5 stars.

The user can be the original author of the review or an administrator with appropriate permissions. The operation will validate that the current user has permission to update the review before proceeding with the change. No other fields (such as product code, review code, or creation date) can be updated via this operation.

id.description: Unique identifier for a product category. Assigned by the system during creation and is immutable. Format follows standard UUID representation. This serves as the primary key and identifies the category in all catalog operations, enabling consistent reference across all platform features.

name.description: Official name of the product category. This is the primary identifier used in the product catalog and displayed to customers during product browsing. Names must be unique within the platform to prevent confusion during product organization and categorization.

description.description: Detailed description of the product category, explaining its purpose, typical products included, and usage scenarios. This description is used for SEO optimization and customer guidance in shopping experiences, helping users understand the category's relevance to their needs.

parentCategory.description: Parent category object that the current category belongs to in the category hierarchy. Represents the hierarchical positioning of the category, with the top-level categories having no parent. The reference uses the summary version to prevent circular references and reduce payload size, enabling efficient listing and embedding.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the category was initially recorded in the database. This serves as an immutable creation marker, critical for audit trails, historical analysis of catalog changes, and version control mechanisms.

IShoppingMallProductCategory.description: Product category entity representing a specific organizational unit for products in the shopping platform. Categories define the catalog structure and serve as fundamental building blocks for product indexing, filtering, and discovery features. Each category establishes a hierarchical relationship with either a parent category or exists as a top-level structure, forming the complete category tree. The category system must balance business needs for flexible product organization with user experience considerations to ensure intuitive product browsing. This entity enables comprehensive access to all relevant category information without exposing sensitive or system-managed fields. The response includes all non-sensitive attributes required for product catalog functions, with hierarchical relationships accurately representing the category's position within the platform's organizational structure.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the administrative account within the shopping mall system. This UUID is generated automatically on account creation and serves as the primary key for all database operations involving this entity. The format is strictly UUID version 4 to ensure global uniqueness and compatibility with the database index.

Used in all API endpoints as the unique identifier for administrative accounts, including the pagination endpoint that returns this summary type.

The field is read-only and cannot be modified through API operations, as the system manages unique IDs for security and data integrity reasons.

username.description:
A person's chosen display name assigned to their administrative account. A valid username must be between 3-20 characters, consisting of alphanumeric characters and underscores with no spaces or special characters. This field is read-only for security reasons, as usernames should not be changeable once set to maintain historical reference.

Used as a public-facing identifier for administrative accounts in user management interfaces, communications, and activity logs.

Username validation begins during account creation and includes a uniqueness check to prevent conflicts with existing accounts.

email.description:
The primary email address used for communications and account verification. Must be a valid email format per RFC 5322 standards and is a required field for all administrative accounts. The email is verified during account creation and serves as the primary means of authentication recovery.

This email is used in the authentication process and display across platform interfaces for administrative purposes.

Email addresses cannot be changed by the user through the public API; only through administrative actions in the system.

last_login_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent successful authentication attempt by the administrator. This field is optional during creation (will be populated automatically on first login) but becomes mandatory for all subsequent operations. Recorded in ISO 8601 format (date-time) for consistent date comparisons and sorting in administrative interfaces.

Used to determine account activity levels, generate activity reports, and assess potential security risks through login patterns.

Automatically updated on every successful authentication attempt and available for filtering and sorting in administrative management interfaces.

is_active.description:
Boolean flag indicating whether the administrative account is currently enabled for use. When true, the account can perform system operations. When false, the account is locked for all system access. This value is controlled by administrative action through the user management interface, not by client-side modification.

Used in the pagination response to filter active administrative accounts for management operations.

The field is not exposed to the API for user modification; it's managed through dedicated admin set account status endpoints.

IShoppingMallAdmin.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of an administrative account in the ShoppingMall platform. This type contains abbreviated but essential information about an administrator, optimized for list display and context in management interfaces.

Designed for use in paginated responses from the GET /shoppingMall/admin/admins endpoint. The summary provides necessary account details while omitting sensitive information like password hashes and session tokens to ensure security and performance.

This DTO type follows the IShoppingMallAdmin.ISummary pattern, containing ID, username, and email fields as mandatory information, while allowing additional fields like last_login_at and is_active to be null where applicable.

IShoppingMallProductImage.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a product image, providing essential information for display in product galleries.

This type is used in paginated responses to list product images with minimal fields, optimized for performance when displaying multiple images in a catalog or search result interface.

The summary includes basic image identification (ID and URLs), display order properties, and accessibility metadata, excluding complex fields like full description, creation timestamps, or database references to avoid redundant data in list views.

This summary type does not contain embedded object relations or composition fields, as it is designed specifically for list display. The full image details, including complete metadata and relationships, would be retrieved via a separate endpoint when needed for detailed user interactions, such as viewing an image in a product gallery with additional information.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the product image within the database, following UUID format.

This primary key is generated automatically during image creation and remains constant throughout the image's lifecycle in the system.

The UUID format ensures uniqueness across all product images within the entire application, eliminating the risk of ID collisions even with high volume image processing.

This identifier should not be used for business logic or content purposes - it exists solely for database and API reference. All business-facing image identification should use the file name or file URL, not the ID.

fileUrl.description:
Full URL pointing to the actual image file hosted on the media server or CDN, properly formatted as a URI.

This URL is directly consumed by frontend applications to render the image in product galleries, search results, and related UI components.

The URL must be publicly accessible without authentication and must conform to standard URI format (e.g., https://domain.com/images/product-42.jpg), with valid scheme and proper encoding.

The URL should not include user-specific tokens or temporary authentication mechanisms, ensuring consistent access for all authenticated users.

fileName.description:
Full name of the image file including the extension (e.g., 'product-42-image-1.jpg').

This filename should exactly match the file's name on the server to ensure proper asset linking, without modifications to the original name.

The filename should be descriptive of the image content for accessibility purposes (e.g., 'main-product-view', 'product-variant-color'), but should not exceed 128 characters for performance and database management reasons.

This filename is used to identify the exact file on disk or storage, and is not intended for direct business display to users.

fileExtension.description:
File extension (e.g., 'jpg', 'png') without the dot character, derived from the filename.

This extension is used to determine the appropriate MIME type and content format for the image when displayed in the browser.

File extensions should be standard, case-insensitive format (e.g., 'JPG' is not standard, 'jpg' should be used), and must be between 2-5 characters in length.

The file extension should not be used for business logic and should primarily serve as a technical identifier for content handling.

description.description:
Minimal accessibility description of the image content for screen readers, SEO, and accessibility compliance.

This field contains a concise natural language description of the image's content, optimized for screen reader users and search engine indexing (e.g., 'Product image showing the front view of the blue laptop computer').

Descriptions must be limited to 255 characters to maintain performance, ensure consistency across the platform, and prevent excessive data in API responses.

This description is not meant for user-facing display but for accessibility and search optimization, with direct reference to the product imagery being displayed.

displayOrder.description:
Numeric value determining the display order rank for the image within the product gallery view.

A lower numerical value indicates an earlier position in the display sequence, with the first image (typically the primary image) having a value of 0 or 1 depending on the configuration.

This value must be a non-negative integer to ensure consistent ordering logic in the client application, with 0 being the typical value for the primary image.

Display order is used to determine the sequence of images in galleries, product pages, and related UI components, but does not affect business-critical data.

isPrimary.description:
Flag indicating whether this image should be used as the primary product image in the product's main gallery.

A value of true indicates this image is designated as the main product image for display on product pages and search results.

A value of false indicates this image is part of the standard gallery but should not be shown as the primary image (it might be shown as a secondary image in a gallery view).

This flag directly impacts the user experience of product display, with only one primary image expected per product.

IShoppingMallProductSpec.ICreate.description:
Product specification details to create for the shopping mall platform. This schema represents the technical details, dimensions, and materials information that sellers provide for their product variants, making it visible to customers on product detail pages. The specifications directly associate with a specific product (identified by productCode in the request path) and are stored in the ProductSpec database table, linking variant specifications to their parent product for comprehensive product catalog management.

The technical specifications include detailed attributes about the product variant, such as dimensions (width, height, depth), materials used, weight specifications, and additional technical data that helps customers make informed purchasing decisions. These specifications serve as an essential component of the product detail page, enhancing product understanding and trust in the marketplace.

This schema is designed for seller operations only - the authentication context (seller identity) is automatically provided by the system via the JWT token (seller_id field is excluded from this schema as it's handled by authentication context).

name.description: Clear and concise name for the specification type (e.g., 'Material Composition', 'Dimensions', 'Weight Specifications'). This name helps organize and categorize technical details for customers on the product detail page. Must include a meaningful label that directly describes the type of specification it represents.

description.description: Detailed explanation of the specification content, which will be displayed to customers on the product detail page. This should include comprehensive technical information that helps shoppers understand the product's attributes and specifications in depth, such as material composition details, dimensional measurements, or specific feature explanations. Must be written at a level accessible to a general consumer audience.

value.description: The actual technical data value for this specification. This is the concrete data point that appears on the product page (e.g., '5.5" x 3" x 2"', '100% cotton', '1.2kg'). Represents the specific value of the specification as it would be displayed to customers on the product detail page.

order.description: Determines the display order of the specification on the product detail page. Specifications with lower order values appear first in the list. Must be positive integer to ensure specifications appear in proper sequence to customers, and prevent duplicate order values to avoid rendering inconsistencies.

rating.description:
Product rating value between 1 and 5 representing customer's satisfaction on a scale. Must be a number between 1 and 5 inclusive.

The system validates minimum rating of 1 and maximum rating of 5 as defined in business rules. Ratings are used to calculate the product's average rating, which directly influences buyer purchase decisions and product visibility in search results.

The rating is displayed to customers as a 5-star scale, where 1 star indicates poor satisfaction and 5 stars indicates excellent satisfaction.

comment.description:
Customer's descriptive feedback about the product. Must be at least 10 characters long to prevent trivial reviews.

The system enforces minimum 10-character length as per business rules for meaningful customer feedback. Comments are subject to content moderation to prevent offensive language or inappropriate content.

This field contains the actual user-generated text that appears on the product page, providing potential customers with detailed insights about their experience with the product.
comment.example: This product exceeded my expectations with great build quality and excellent functionality.

IShoppingMallProductReview.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new product review. Contains required rating and comment fields without any actor or reference fields since authentication context is provided through standard authorization.

Follows atomic operation principle by including all necessary data for a single review creation call. The rating field's value directly affects the product's average rating calculation, which is displayed to customers on the product page.

Customer comments must contain a minimum of 10 characters to ensure meaningful feedback is provided, and all comments are processed through content moderation filters before being published to the platform.

IShoppingMallProductSpec.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of product specification details optimized for list representation in product spec listings. Provides essential fields without heavy composition data to ensure efficient performance during list operations and pagination.

This summary type contains the key attributes of product specifications while omitting large text fields and nested arrays related to specification detail. It's designed for both product listing views and rapid identification of spec entries in service contexts.

The product reference field is implemented as IShoppingMallProduct.ISummary to maintain data consistency and prevent circular reference issues while providing necessary product context.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the product specification entry. This serves as the primary key for the database record and enables precise identification of specifications during operations.

UUID format ensures global uniqueness across the system, making it suitable for referential integrity and automatic record tracking by the backend without dependency on user-provided values.

product.description:
Summary representation of the product to which this specification belongs. Provides the core product context without including full composition data.

Including a summary reference instead of full product details prevents circular reference issues while still providing essential context for the product specification listing.

attribute.description:
Name of the attribute this specification details. Represents the specific technical characteristic that is being defined, such as 'Color', 'Material', or 'Size'.

This should be a human-readable term that clearly describes the specification aspect without including values or technical implementation details.

value.description:
Value assigned to the attribute for this specification. Contains the specific instance value, such as 'Red', 'Cotton', or 'Medium'.

This field represents the actual data point that defines the specific product specification in accordance with the attribute name.

version.description:
Specification version identifier for tracking changes. Used to manage evolving specification formats and maintain version compatibility between different versions.

When specification schemas evolve, this field allows the system to identify the schema version used, ensuring schema compatibility when handling historical specification data.

id.description: Unique product identifier generated upon product creation. This is the system's primary key for tracking the product across all operations. The ID is immutable once assigned and cannot be changed after creation to ensure data integrity for all related operations.

name.description:
Product name visible to customers in lists and search results. This should be the marketing name, not internal SKU or code. The name should be concise but descriptive enough for customers to easily recognize the product, typically limited to 50 characters for optimal display across all devices.

This field is required for listing products in search results and category pages to provide users with immediate name recognition without requiring additional clicks.

short_description.description:
Concise product description of 50-100 characters providing essential product information. This is a shortened version of the full description that highlights the key selling point.

The shortened description helps customers quickly identify the product's purpose and major features without requiring them to view more details, improving browsing experience and conversion rates.

price.description:
Current selling price for the product in the site's base currency. Represents the active price at time of query, which may be different from historical prices due to promotions or inventory changes.

This price is formatted as a number with up to two decimal places (e.g., 99.99), which aligns with standard pricing conventions for e-commerce platforms and avoids ambiguity in monetary amounts.

category.description:
Category to which product belongs, providing contextual organization. This reference to the category summary is optimized for catalog display and navigation.

The category relationship is important for users trying to browse similar products and helps organize the catalog into intuitive sections for better user experience and discoverability.

image_url.description:
URL of a thumbnail image showing the product, suitable for display in catalog views. The image should be 300x300 pixels or smaller to optimize loading time for multiple items simultaneously.

Image URLs are generated upon product upload and serve as the primary visual identifier in product listings, making it the first element customers notice when browsing through product categories.

reviews_count.description:
Total count of customer reviews for the product, updated in real-time. This number helps customers gauge product popularity and community reception before making a purchase.

This field is critical for social proof and is calculated directly from the review database, providing customers with an immediate understanding of how many people have purchased and reviewed the product.

rating_average.description:
Average customer rating for the product, calculated from all reviews. This is a floating-point value typically between 1 and 5.0, displayed as a number for precise scoring.

The average rating serves as a key purchasing decision factor for customers, with higher averages generally correlating with increased purchase probability. It's calculated with precision down to two decimal places.

IShoppingMallProduct.ISummary.description:
Product summary object optimized for catalog display in search results and category pages. Contains all necessary information for listing while excluding detailed specifications to improve performance and user experience in list views.

This summary includes critical visual information through image_url, essential pricing data through price, category context through category, and social proof through reviews_count and rating_average. All fields are designed for efficient rendering in list-based interfaces, keeping data size minimal.

id.description: Unique identifier for the login attempt record. Auto-generated by the system and used to reference specific log entries for further investigation or correlation with other security data.

userId.description: Identifier of the user who attempted the login. This represents the account being targeted in the failed authentication attempt.

ip.description: IP address from which the login attempt originated. Used to identify potential source locations for security threats and track attack patterns.

attemptedAt.description: Timestamp of when the login attempt occurred in ISO 8601 format. Used to understand the timing of security incidents for trend analysis.

failureReason.description: Description of why the login attempt failed, such as incorrect password, account locked, or expired session. Provides immediate context for security personnel to understand the nature of the attempt.

IShoppingMallLoginAttempt.ISummary.description: Login attempt summary representing failed authentication attempts for security monitoring. This summary provides essential details to help administrators identify potential security threats without exposing sensitive authentication details. Each attempt record includes the user identifier (from the relevant user account), originating IP address, failure reason, and timestamp of the failed attempt. This summary type is optimized for list views and security analytics dashboards, containing minimally sufficient information for quick triage of security incidents.

IShoppingMallProduct.IUpdate.description:
DTO for updating specific product attributes of a seller-managed item. This partial update allows sellers to modify non-structural aspects of their product listings, preserving the product code and associated seller relationships. The request must exclude any fields that are system-managed or require authentication context validation.

The product update operation allows for partial field updates, where only the specified fields in the request body are modified. The product code, creation date, and seller ID remain unchanged as they are either in the path parameter or provided by the authentication context.

This DTO specifically targets the update endpoint for sellers, ensuring that the request contains only valid, updatable fields without violating security principles regarding authentication and authorization.

name.description: Product display name visible to customers. Updated name must follow naming conventions, avoiding special characters and exceeding maximum length of 255 characters. This field is optional in the update request, representing the current product name when omitted from the payload. Name updates are logged for change history tracking with timestamped versioning.

description.description: Detailed product description used for marketing and listing. Must be SEO-friendly and follow industry standards for clarity and conciseness. Maximum length is 2000 characters to ensure optimal display across all platform views. Description updates automatically trigger re-indexing in search services to reflect content changes across all listings.

price.description: Product price in platform currency units. Must be non-negative and can be updated to reflect current market conditions. Price updates are subject to currency conversion rules and validation logic to prevent invalid amounts. Prices are displayed with two decimal places during customer-facing interactions.

isActive.description: Indicates whether the product is available for sale. When set to false, product is hidden from customer views but remains in database for historical tracking. This status change is logged for auditing purposes, providing a record of when and why the product was paused or resumed in the marketplace.

IShoppingMallProductImage.ICreate.description:
Product image creation request schema for seller's product images. This schema represents the metadata and file reference needed to associate an image with a product during creation. The schema aligns with database schema 'shopping_mall_product_images' and follows DTO creation patterns for sellers.

This schema is used in the POST /shoppingMall/seller/products/{productCode}/images endpoint to upload new product images. It contains all necessary fields for image association, while excluding any authentication or session fields which are handled by the backend via JWT authentication.

url.description:
The public URL where the image file is stored. This URL must be accessible to the frontend and used for image display.

The URL references the hosted image location, typically a CDN or storage service. The system does not process the file - it stores the URL as provided.

Valid URLs must follow standard URI format with http or https schemes, like 'https://cdn.example.com/images/product_image.jpg'.

position.description:
Index position of the image within the product gallery. Images with lower positions appear first in the gallery.

If not provided, the system defaults to position 0 (primary image). Position values must be sequential integers starting from 0.

Typically, the first image created becomes position 0 (primary image), next becomes 1, etc. This field is optional on creation - it can be updated later.

altText.description:
Alternative text for accessibility purposes, describing the image content for screen readers or when images don't load.

The alt text should provide a concise description of the image content, such as 'Blue leather handbag with gold accents'. This is crucial for accessibility compliance.

Long descriptions exceeding 255 characters will be truncated and may cause accessibility issues if not properly prepared.

example.altText: Blue leather handbag with gold accents

IShoppingMallSection.ICreate.description:
DTO for creating a new sales channel section. This data object is specifically used by the section creation API endpoint to define the structure of the request body. It contains only the essential fields required for establishing a new section within a sales channel, including the user-visible name, positioning order within the channel, and the channel ID that defines the context for section organization.

The name field must be a clear, descriptive string for customer-facing visibility, with length constraints to ensure UI compatibility. Position represents the sort order for the section within its channel, requiring a positive integer to prevent display conflicts. Channel_id establishes the relationship with an existing sales channel in the database, validated before creation to maintain data integrity.

This DTO is designed for administrative use only, excluding system-managed fields like IDs and timestamps. All validation rules are enforced at the API layer to maintain consistent section structures across the platform. The fields included directly correspond to the critical attributes necessary for section creation as defined in the database schema and API specifications.

name.description:
The user-facing name of the section that appears in the platform interface. Must be a meaningful string representing the purpose or category of content within the section, such as 'Summer Collection' or 'New Arrivals'.

The name should provide clear context to customers without being overly long or ambiguous. Valid values are strings between 1-255 characters, with no empty strings or spaces only.

position.description:
The sequence position of the section within its sales channel. Determines the visual order displayed on the channel page (lower numbers appear before higher numbers).

Must be a positive integer greater than zero to avoid negative positioning and ensure sorting alignment. This value must be unique within its channel to prevent display conflicts and maintain logical channel structure.

channel_id.description:
The identifier of the sales channel to which this section belongs. This field references the shopping_mall_channels table and must match an existing channel ID to prevent orphaned sections.

The sales channel context is required to determine where the section will appear within the platform. The platform validates this ID before record creation.

IShoppingMallEmailVerificationToken.ISum.description:
Summary representation of an email verification token, designed specifically for listing and administrative review.

This type provides essential visual and status information in user lists without exposing sensitive data. It includes basic identification details, expiration timing, and verification status to enable efficient administrative workflows related to email verification processes.

The summary excludes sensitive token values, detailed user information, and administrative notes to maintain security and focus on essential fields for quick review of token status.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the email verification token, used to reference and manage the token in system operations.

This ID is an immutable, system-generated identifier that represents the verification token internally. It follows UUID v4 format and is required for operations like token lookup, updating status, or deleting tokens.

email.description:
Email address associated with the verification token, displayed in administrative lists for quick identification.

This is the email address for which verification is required. It's a valid email format and is included in the summary because it's essential information for administrators to identify what email the token is for.

expires_at.description:
Timestamp when the email verification token expires, used to display token validity in administrative interface.

This timestamp indicates when the token will no longer be valid for email verification. It's critical for administrators to know when tokens become invalid. If a token is about to expire, the token may need manual follow-up to prevent verification failures for users.

verified_at.description:
Timestamp when the email address associated with the verification token was successfully verified, if applicable.

This field contains the exact date and time when the email verification was completed. It will display as null if the verification hasn't occurred yet. It's used by administrators to determine the verification state of the email and is particularly helpful during troubleshooting for verification issues.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the verification token was created, used for chronological organization of tokens in administrative views.

This timestamp reflects the date and time when the verification token was generated in the system. It's essential for understanding when the token was created, which can inform administrative decisions about token expiration times and account management workflows.

IShoppingMallLowStockAlert.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a low stock alert configuration specifically designed for rendering in administrative list views and summary-based API responses.

This type contains all essential information needed to display low stock alert status in a compact format without including unnecessary detail or composition data. It's optimized for performance when listing multiple alert configurations simultaneously, such as in dashboard views or maintenance interfaces.

Key characteristics:
- Includes only required fields for listing purposes (id, product reference, threshold, etc.)
- Uses summary objects for referenced entities to prevent data bloat
- Excludes detailed administrative information and sensitivity considerations
- Contains operational statuses for quick assessment of alert effectiveness
- Optimized for small payloads while maintaining full business meaning.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the low stock alert record. Generated automatically by the system upon creation.

This field represents the primary key in the database table and is used to reference this specific alert configuration across all system endpoints. It follows standard UUID format to ensure uniqueness and prevent guessing attacks.

product_variant.description:
Reference to the product variant associated with this low stock alert configuration.

This is a summary object containing minimal information about the product variant. It represents the entity relationship without including detailed composition data, as this is a summary type. The summary form includes only essential information for listing purposes.

threshold.description:
Minimum stock level threshold that triggers the alert.

This value is set by administrators to identify when a product variant's inventory level becomes critical. The system monitors real-time inventory and triggers notifications when stock level falls below this threshold. It must be a positive integer value.

current_stock_level.description:
Current inventory count for the product variant that this alert applies to.

This value represents the most recent inventory count from the system's records. It's updated in real-time as inventory levels change, providing administrators with the most current information for decision-making.

oneOf.description:
Current operational status of this low stock alert.

The alert can be active (monitoring and triggering notifications), disabled (not monitoring but retained), or archived (no longer active but kept for historical records). This field determines whether the system will process inventory changes against this alert configuration.

Current operational status of this low stock alert.

The alert can be active (monitoring and triggering notifications), disabled (not monitoring but retained), or archived (no longer active but kept for historical records). This field determines whether the system will process inventory changes against this alert configuration.

The alert can be active (monitoring and triggering notifications), disabled (not monitoring but retained), or archived (no longer active but kept for historical records). This field determines whether the system will process inventory changes against this alert configuration.

alert_status.description:
Current operational status of this low stock alert.

The alert can be active (monitoring and triggering notifications), disabled (not monitoring but retained), or archived (no longer active but kept for historical records). This field determines whether the system will process inventory changes against this alert configuration.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp of the most recent triggering of this alert.

Represents the exact datetime when the system last detected inventory levels below the threshold and triggered the configured notifications. This helps administrators track alert activity and effectiveness. The value is null if the alert has never triggered.

last_triggered.description:
Timestamp of the most recent triggering of this alert.

Represents the exact datetime when the system last detected inventory levels below the threshold and triggered the configured notifications. This helps administrators track alert activity and effectiveness. The value is null if the alert has never triggered.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this alert configuration was created in the system.

This field is automatically set by the system upon creation and represents the moment the alert configuration was first established in the platform.

IShoppingMallLoginAttempt.description:
Detailed record of an individual login attempt for security monitoring and analysis purposes.

This DTO represents a single login event with detailed technical information, including the attempt time, user context, IP address, success status, and failure details when applicable. Intended for security personnel to investigate authentication events and identify potential security threats.

The schema reflects the structure of the shopping_mall_login_attempts database table that tracks authentication events, including all relevant security-related data points essential for forensic analysis. Designed to be the main entity type for these records, providing all necessary information for security analysis.

id.description:
Unique identifier assigned to this login attempt record.

This ID uniquely identifies the login attempt and is used to track the specific event in the security audit system. It's a UUID format string generated automatically by the system when the login attempt is first recorded.

Used as the primary key in the database and for referencing this specific event in API resources and logs. Ensure the UUID is properly formatted as per RFC 4122.

user_id.description:
Identifier of the user account that attempted login.

This field links the login attempt to the specific user account that was targeted during the authentication process. The value corresponds to the 'id' field of the 'shopping_mall_customers' or 'shopping_mall_sellers' table, depending on the user type.

Used by security teams to identify which user account was targeted in the attempt. Provides context for investigation into potential unauthorized access attempts against specific user accounts.

ip_address.description:
IP address of the device that initiated the login attempt.

This field contains the IP address from which the authentication attempt was made, captured from the client's request. The value is an IPv4 address in standard dotted-decimal format (e.g., 192.168.1.1), though IPv6 may be handled via the same field format in some cases.

Helps security teams identify geographical locations or blocked IP ranges. May be masked for sensitive information but must be captured for full forensic analysis.

attempt_timestamp.description:
Timestamp of the login attempt in ISO 8601 format.

This field records the precise moment when the authentication attempt was made, captured in UTC time and formatted as ISO 8601 (e.g., 2022-01-15T10:00:00Z). The value represents the system time when the attempt was first recorded.

Critical for correlating events with other security logs and temporal analysis. The precision enables detailed investigation into potential brute force attacks across time spans.

success.description:
Indicates whether the login attempt was successful.

This boolean value is true if the authentication was successful (user provided correct credentials), and false if authentication failed (incorrect credentials, account lockout, etc.).

Primary indicator for whether the attempt was malicious or legitimate. Used to filter and sort security events in analysis tools.

failure_reason.description:
Provides detailed information about why an authentication attempt failed.

This field contains human-readable error messages that explain the authentication failure reason to security personnel. It's not populated when the login attempt was successful (success: true), meaning it's only relevant when success: false.

The values should be clear, non-technical messages that help security teams quickly understand the nature of the failure, such as 'Incorrect password' or 'Account locked due to multiple failures'. Avoid exposing internal error codes to prevent helping attackers.

This field supports security analysis by providing immediate visibility into the type of authentication failure, aiding in identifying potential security threats.

user_agent.description:
User agent string from the client browser or application.

This field captures the user agent string from the HTTP request header, containing information about the client application, browser, and operating system used during the login attempt (e.g., 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/91.0.4472.124 Safari/537.36').

Helps identify using which client software the attempt was made. Useful for distinguishing between legitimate user activity and automated attack attempts.

attempt_count.description:
Number of consecutive failed login attempts for the user account.

This field tracks the current number of failed login attempts for the user account associated with the attempt. It helps detect and prevent brute force attacks.

Used internally within the authentication system for implementing account lockout policies. Monitor this value to determine if account lockout thresholds have been reached.

oneOf.description:
Image upload process status indicating the current state of the image file processing. This field is managed by the image processing system and reflects the current stage in the upload workflow (uploaded = file received but not processed, processing = file being processed, verified = processing complete and image ready for display, failed = processing failed and image is unusable.

This status is primarily used to provide feedback to the seller about the image's readiness for display. Images with 'failed' status should not be displayed in product listings until the seller resolves the issue. The status is updated automatically during the image processing workflow and can be changed through the API only when the seller requests a re-upload or reprocessing.

This field must be one of four valid values from the predefined enum: 'uploaded', 'processing', 'verified', or 'failed'.

is_visible.description:
Flag indicating whether the product image is visible to customers in the product catalog or store. A visible image can be displayed in the product gallery, while hidden images are not visible on the product page but may still be stored for administrative purposes.

Sellers can toggle visibility to organize images, hide inappropriate images, or temporarily remove images before they are fully processed. This flag is separate from upload status and affects only the display of the image in the catalog, not its processing state.

When a seller sets is_visible=true, the image becomes available in the catalog immediately. Setting to false removes the image from the active gallery.

For product images, this field defaults to true on creation. Sellers can change visibility at any time without affecting other image properties.

position.description:
Numeric value determining the display order of the image within the product gallery. A lower position number means the image appears earlier in the gallery, with position 0 being the first image in the sequence. Positions must be unique within the product and must not be negative.

This field allows sellers to control the visual presentation of the product, highlighting the most important images at the beginning of the gallery. Valid positions are integers that don't conflict with other images in the same product - the system will automatically reorder remaining images when a new position is set.

Position values are updated when the image is modified, but the system will handle repositioning of other images to prevent overlaps or out-of-range positions.

IShoppingMallProductImage.IUpdate.description:
Product image metadata update schema for sellers to adjust image properties within product listings. This DTO allows sellers to update visibility, upload status, and display position of product images without having to provide the entire image metadata. The update operation replaces the specified image's metadata fields with the provided values, maintaining the existing image URL and file information.

The schema reflects the database model structure for product images, excluding fields that are managed by the system or derived from the authentication context. Since this is an update operation, only the fields that can be modified by the seller are included, and all fields are optional to provide flexibility in partial updates.

Used for updating image metadata through the product image PUT endpoint, which requires seller authentication and validation that the product and image belong to the same product entity. The update will fail if the specified productCode or imageCode do not match any existing product-image relationship.

IShoppingMallLowStockAlert.IRequest.description:
Configuration parameters for modifying low stock alert settings including threshold values and notification preferences.

This request body supports partial updates to alert configurations, allowing administrators to modify specific parameters like minimum stock thresholds, notification frequency, and enabled status without affecting other configuration settings. The system processes these updates incrementally without requiring full configuration replacement.

All fields are optional to support targeted updates - the system only modifies the parameters that are included in the request.

threshold.description: The minimum inventory threshold below which low stock alerts will be triggered. This value must reflect the actual stock quantity required for alerts. For product variants without specific thresholds, the system uses organizational defaults from the configuration settings.

notificationEnabled.description: Enables or disables the entire low stock alert system for this configuration. When enabled, the system will monitor inventory levels and trigger alerts according to the defined thresholds and notification settings. When disabled, no alerts are generated regardless of inventory levels.

oneOf.description: How frequently the system checks inventory levels and triggers alerts. Valid options are 'immediate' (checks continuously), 'daily' (checks once per day), 'weekly' (checks once per week), or 'monthly' (checks once per month). The default is 'daily' when not specified.
