notificationFrequency.description: How frequently the system checks inventory levels and triggers alerts. Valid options are 'immediate' (checks continuously), 'daily' (checks once per day), 'weekly' (checks once per week), or 'monthly' (checks once per month). The default is 'daily' when not specified.

emailNotification.description: Enables or disables email notifications for low stock alerts. When enabled, alerts are sent to the configured email addresses. This setting can be changed independently of other notification channels.

inAppNotification.description: Enables or disables in-application notifications for low stock alerts. When enabled, users receive alerts within the application interface without requiring email. This setting can be changed independently of email notification settings.

IShoppingMallProductImage.IRequest.description:
Pagination and filtering parameters for product image list operations. Supports querying product images with configurable page size, sort order, and text search based on product images metadata and associated product details.

Configurable parameters allow frontend applications to implement efficient client-side pagination and dynamic filtering without requiring multiple separate API calls. The parameters follow standard REST conventions for paginated data, ensuring compatibility across client implementations.

This request type is used in both customer and seller product image listing endpoints to provide consistent API experience and maintainable codebase. The parameters are designed to be minimal yet expressive, covering the essential needs for image listing requests in the e-commerce platform.

page.description:
Page number of results to return. Must be a positive integer starting from 1.

Values below 1 should be interpreted as 1 (defaulting to first page). The parameter ensures the API only returns data for the specified page of results, preventing over-fetching of unnecessary records.

In the context of image galleries, this parameter supports infinite scroll patterns and traditional pagination controls, allowing users to navigate through potentially large image collections efficiently.

limit.description:
Number of items per page. Must be a positive integer with a maximum value of 100.

This limits the response size to ensure manageable data transfers for both client and server. Default value of 10 is typically used if not specified, but the operation requires it to be explicitly provided in the request for clarity.

For product image listings, typical values range from 10-50 items per page, balancing between loading speed and sufficient image display depth without overwhelming the user interface.

sort_by.description:
Field to sort results by. Possible values include 'created_at' (default), 'display_order', and 'filename'.

The sorting field must correspond to existing database columns to maintain API consistency. This parameter allows developers to implement client-side sorting while maintaining server-side data integrity.

In the context of product images, sorting by 'display_order' makes the most sense for image galleries and product views, while 'created_at' may be useful for administrative interfaces.

oneOf.description:
Sort direction. Valid values are 'asc' (ascending) and 'desc' (descending). Default is 'asc'.

This parameter works in conjunction with 'sort_by' to determine the sequence of results. The 'desc' order is commonly used for recent activity or newest images.

Product image systems often prefer descending order for recently added images, while ascending order might be used for chronological display of image addition dates.

This parameter works in conjunction with 'sort_by' to determine the sequence of results. The 'desc' order is commonly used for recent activity or newest images.

Product image systems often prefer descending order for recently added images, while ascending order might be used for chronological display of image addition dates.

search.description:
Text to search for in associated product data. Searches across product names, categories, and image file names.

This parameter enables clients to implement simple search functionality without requiring complex API endpoints. The search is implemented with a basic substring match to the product's fields.

When a valid search term is provided, the API performs a partial match on relevant product data fields, allowing users to quickly locate images related to specific products or attributes.

page.description:
Page number for pagination. Must be a positive integer. The first page is 1. Required parameter for pagination.

This indicates which page of results the client wants to see. The service uses this parameter to calculate the offset for the database query. The client should provide a page number starting at 1, and the service will return records starting from that offset.

limit.description:
Number of records per page. Must be between 1 and 100. Default value is 20.

The service limits results to 100 per page for performance reasons. The client can choose a smaller number for more detailed views, but a value over 100 will be automatically capped at 100. A value of 0 is not allowed, as it would return no results.

sortBy.description:
Field name to sort results by (e.g., 'timestamp', 'eventType').

Valid sort fields include 'timestamp' for chronological order and 'eventType' for categorizing event types. The service will sort results based on these fields in the specified order. If this parameter is omitted, the service will default to sorting by timestamp in descending order.

oneOf.description:
Sorting direction. Must be either 'asc' for ascending or 'desc' for descending.

This parameter works in conjunction with sortBy to determine the sorting order. For example, sorting by timestamp in ascending order will return the oldest entries first, while descending returns the newest first. The default sorting direction depends on how the service was designed, but this parameter overrides the default.

IShoppingMallInventoryLog.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for retrieving inventory audit log entries with pagination and sorting capabilities. This DTO is used to filter and paginate the complete inventory log history records for system administrators.

Pagination parameters include page number and page size, allowing administrators to load data in manageable chunks for efficient performance. Sorting capabilities enable administrators to organize logs by timestamp or event type for easier auditing.

The parameters are designed for the backend to efficiently handle database queries for inventory auditing purposes with clear, business-friendly naming standards.

IShoppingMallVariantInventories.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for fetching product variant inventory records. Supports filtering by product ID, variant ID, and minimum stock levels, with optional pagination and sorting. Designed for sellers to efficiently monitor and manage inventory across product variants.

The search filters inventory records to provide relevant stock availability information. Sellers can view inventory health by defining minimum stock thresholds, which helps identify items needing restocking. Pagination allows efficient data loading for large inventory datasets.

This object does NOT include any ID fields that would indicate a specific variant, but contains properties to filter the inventory listings.

Inventory search parameters are critical for sellers managing product listings in the shopping platform. Proper configuration of these parameters directly impacts the efficiency of daily inventory management operations and the accuracy of stock visibility.

page.description:
The page number of results to retrieve (1-based index). A value of 1 represents the first page of results. This parameter is used to implement pagination for large result sets.

Pagination is essential for efficient data retrieval in inventory management systems, especially when dealing with extensive product variant datasets. By breaking results into manageable pages, sellers can quickly scan inventory status without overwhelming system resources or browser performance.

limit.description:
The number of items to return per page. The maximum allowed value is 100 to prevent overloading. A default value of 20 is used if not specified.

This parameter directly affects data transfer size and response times for inventory operations. The default value of 20 provides an optimal balance between result visibility and performance, minimizing page load times while keeping enough items visible for informed decision-making.

product_id.description:
Filter variant inventories by specific product ID. When provided, only inventory records related to this product will be included in results. This allows sellers to view inventory status for a particular product they're managing.

Product ID filtering is critical for sellers managing specific products in their catalog. It enables targeted inventory checks without requiring extensive filtering through the full product catalog, improving operational efficiency when managing individual items.

variant_id.description:
Filter variant inventories by specific variant ID. When provided, only inventory records for this product variant will be included. This enables sellers to view the stock level of a specific variant.

Variant-specific filtering allows sellers to monitor stock levels for specific product options (color, size, etc.) without navigating through the full catalog. It's particularly valuable during restocking planning for individual variants.

min_stock_level.description:
Minimum stock level threshold to filter inventory records. Only variants with stock quantity at or above this threshold will be returned. This helps sellers identify inventory that meets their minimum stocking requirements.

The minimum stock level setting is a critical business parameter for inventory management. It helps sellers maintain optimal stock levels that balance customer satisfaction (avoiding stockouts) with cost efficiency (avoiding excessive inventory), directly impacting profitability.

oneOf.description: The field to sort the results by. Valid options include product name, variant name, and current stock quantity. Sorting helps sellers organize inventory records for easy scanning and comparison.
The field to sort the results by. Valid options include product name, variant name, and current stock quantity. Sorting helps sellers organize inventory records for easy scanning and comparison.
The field to sort the results by. Valid options include product name, variant name, and current stock quantity. Sorting helps sellers organize inventory records for easy scanning and comparison.

order_by.description:
The field to sort the results by. Valid options include product name, variant name, and current stock quantity. Sorting helps sellers organize inventory records for easy scanning and comparison.

Sorting is a performance-critical feature in inventory management where sellers frequently need to identify understocked or high-demand variants. The sorting field directly impacts the effectiveness of inventory analysis and decision-making.

oneOf.description: Sorting direction for the results. 'asc' means ascending order while 'desc' means descending. The default is ascending order, which lists items from lowest to highest for the chosen order_by field.
Sorting direction for the results. 'asc' means ascending order while 'desc' means descending. The default is ascending order, which lists items from lowest to highest for the chosen order_by field.

direction.description:
Sorting direction for the results. 'asc' means ascending order while 'desc' means descending. The default is ascending order, which lists items from lowest to highest for the chosen order_by field.

Direction selection works in conjunction with sorting fields to provide sellers with the most useful inventory visibility. Ascending orders typically show lower stock levels first (helping identify restock needs), while descending orders list higher quantities first (useful for identifying overstocked items).

IShoppingMallInventoryAdjustment.IUpdate.description: Request DTO for updating specific inventory adjustment records. This type receives partial updates for inventory adjustments, allowing sellers and administrators to modify the quantity, adjustment reason, and status of manual inventory adjustments made for product variants. The schema supports partial updates, so only the fields that need to be changed should be included in the request body. This is used in the PUT /shoppingMall/seller/inventory/adjustments/{adjustmentId} and PUT /shoppingMall/admin/inventory/adjustments/{adjustmentId} operations.

adjustment_quantity.description:
The quantity to adjust in the inventory represents the numerical value of the inventory change, indicating the number of items to be added or subtracted from the product variant's stock. Positive values are used for adding stock (e.g., +50 for restocking), while negative values are used for removing stock (e.g., -10 for damaged items). This quantity must reflect the actual change made in the inventory system, ensuring that the adjustment is accurately recorded for stock reconciliation purposes.

The quantity is a critical field in inventory adjustments as it directly impacts the product variant's available stock. The system enforces a business rule that prevents negative inventory levels after the adjustment, so the quantity must be calculated carefully to reflect actual stock movement. When adjusting inventory, sellers should ensure that the quantity accounts for all items that were received or removed from the warehouse, including any discrepancies reported during cycle counts. Values must represent actual physical inventory movements and cannot be used for administrative accounting purposes.

reason.description:
The adjustment reason provides a detailed explanation for why the inventory modification was necessary, serving as a critical audit trail element for inventory management. This field should include specific information about the inventory event such as 'Restocking after warehouse delivery', 'Damage in transit', 'Seasonal clearance', or 'Inventory count discrepancy' to enable proper tracking and reporting.

This field is mandatory for all adjustments requiring manual intervention and must contain at least 10 characters of meaningful content to prevent vague entries like 'Adjustment made' or 'Fix inventory'. The reason serves as the primary reference point for administrators when reviewing inventory changes, verifying compliance with business policies, and auditing inventory discrepancies. In cases of product damage, the reason should specify the nature of the damage and affected product quantities.

oneOf.description: The initial status when an inventory adjustment is first created. Pending adjustments are awaiting verification by administrators before any inventory changes are applied. Sellers can submit adjustments in PENDING status, but these require manual approval before affecting actual inventory levels.

The status assigned when an inventory adjustment has been verified and approved by an administrator. Approved adjustments have been confirmed as valid and have successfully updated the product variant's inventory levels. This status indicates that the adjustment is complete and reflected in all inventory reports.

The status applied when an inventory adjustment is deemed invalid or unauthorized by administrators. Rejected adjustments do not affect inventory levels and must be corrected before resubmission. This status is typically used when adjustments lack required documentation, reference invalid inventory, or violate inventory policies.

status.description: The new status to be applied to the inventory adjustment record. This field determines the processing state of the adjustment based on the workflow: PENDING (initial submission), APPROVED (verified and applied), or REJECTED (not approved). The status change must follow the documented workflow with clear business justification.

IShoppingMallProductReview.IRequest.description:
Product review request parameters enable efficient data retrieval for client-side display with paginated results. This DTO provides search capabilities including rating thresholds, date range filtering, and configurable sort ordering to support various customer interface requirements without compromising system performance or data integrity.

All pagination parameters have strict validation to protect against unreasonable data loads, with limits enforcing both minimum (1) and maximum (100) values. The date parameters accept ISO 8601 formatted timestamps, while rating filters strictly enforce the 0-5 scale. The default page number is 1 and default limit is 10, ensuring client compatibility with minimal configuration requirements.

page.description: Current page number for pagination. Must be at least 1, with no upper limit specified beyond typical system constraints. A value of 1 represents the first page of results.

limit.description: Number of items to return per page. Defaults to 10 if not provided, with a maximum limit of 100 items per page to prevent excessive data transfer.

sortBy.description: Field to sort results by. Supported values include 'created_at' for chronological ordering and 'rating' for review score ordering, with additional fields possible in future versions.

oneOf.description: Sorting order for sorted fields. 'asc' for ascending order (oldest first, lowest rating), 'desc' for descending order (newest first, highest rating).
Sorting order for sorted fields. 'asc' for ascending order (oldest first, lowest rating), 'desc' for descending order (newest first, highest rating).

order.description: Sorting order for sorted fields. 'asc' for ascending order (oldest first, lowest rating), 'desc' for descending order (newest first, highest rating).

minRating.description: Minimum rating threshold for included reviews. Rating values are on a 0-5 scale, where 5 is highest.

maxRating.description: Maximum rating threshold for included reviews. Rating values are on a 0-5 scale, where 5 is highest.

dateFrom.description: Earliest date for review creation. Reviews created on or after this date will be included in results. Format must comply with ISO 8601 standards.

dateTo.description: Latest date for review creation. Reviews created on or before this date will be included in results. Format must comply with ISO 8601 standards.

id.description: Unique identifier for the low-stock alert, generated automatically by the system for traceability across the inventory monitoring features. The UUID format ensures globally unique references that are suitable for distributed systems without conflict, maintaining referential integrity in audit logs and transaction history. This identifier is immutable and serves as the primary key for accessing alert records.

product.description: Link to the product in the products table (shopping_mall_products), representing the product for which the low-stock alert was triggered. The reference relationship enables direct access to product details such as name, category, and variant information without requiring separate API lookups. This is the transformed relation using .ISummary pattern.

current_stock_level.description: Current inventory count of the product that triggered the alert, representing the real-time stock available in the system prior to the threshold breach. This value must be a positive integer and reflects the actual quantity in stock as counted against active inventory records. The system calculates and updates this value based on recent sales, shipments, and inventory adjustments.

low_stock_threshold.description: Configurable threshold level for the product inventory, below which the system triggers a low-stock alert. This value determines when the alert is generated and should be set by administrators according to business requirements and historical sales patterns. The threshold is product-specific and can be adjusted dynamically to match changing demand.

created_at.description: Timestamp indicating when the low-stock alert was created, recorded using precise ISO 8601 date-time format. This field captures the exact moment the inventory level crossed the configured threshold, providing critical context for inventory review and response planning. The timestamp is automatically generated during alert creation and cannot be modified.

IShoppingMallLowStockAlert.description: Detailed low-stock alert information including product details and alert timestamp. This schema represents a system alert triggered when inventory levels fall below a configured threshold, providing essential details for inventory management and replenishment workflows. The alert uniquely identifies the product (through reference), current stock, and threshold level, with timestamped creation for audit purposes.

IShoppingMallProduct.description:
Product entity representing a catalog item in the shopping mall platform, including all core details required for product listing and catalog display.

This entity captures product metadata including name, description, and pricing, and maintains a reference to the parent category for organizational structure. The product is uniquely identified by a business code that avoids UUIDs in public URLs for better user experience and branding.

The product details include availability status to determine if the product is currently viewable in the catalog. The category reference provides contextual information for product filtering and navigation, using the summary version for efficiency in responses.

All fields are exposed through public endpoints, but no internal system details are included in the response for security and privacy reasons.

id.description: Unique system identifier for the product record, generated internally

code.description: Business code identifier for the product, used in public URLs and marketing materials for uniqueness and branding

name.description: Product name as it appears in the catalog, used for search and visibility

description.description: Detailed product description including features, specifications, and usage instructions

price.description: Product selling price in USD. Must be positive and rounded to two decimal places

category.description: Category the product belongs to in a summary form, providing essential context for catalog organization and filtering. This summary view contains the category identifier and name only for efficient data transfer and better performance in API responses.

isActive.description: Flag indicating whether the product is currently active and available for purchase in the catalog

IShoppingMallInventoryLog.ISummary.description:
Category-level inventory summary for administrative dashboard purposes.

This object aggregates key inventory metrics for product categories in the shopping mall platform. It provides a concise yet comprehensive overview of inventory health across multiple dimensions including current stock, minimum thresholds, low stock alerts, and restocking priorities.

The data is derived from three primary source tables: shopping_mall_variant_inventories (for stock levels), shopping_mall_low_stock_alerts (for threshold configuration), and shopping_mall_product_categories (for category definitions). This summary is designed specifically for the platform administrator dashboard to enable rapid inventory management decisions without requiring additional API calls for context.

The schema follows an optimized structure for performance, with all fields being non-nullable to maximize data reliability in dashboard display scenarios. Each metric is selected for its direct business relevance to inventory management workflows.

IShoppingMallProductCategory.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new product category in the shopping mall platform, used by administrators to organize products into hierarchical structures. This schema defines the necessary and optional fields required for category creation, including category name, optional description, and optional parent category reference for hierarchical organization.

Category creation is restricted to admin users and requires the category name to be unique platform-wide. The schema complies with the platform's data structure requirements and security protocols, excluding any system-managed or authentication-related fields from the request body.

name.description:
The product category name required for this operation. This name is displayed to customers during product browsing and used for filtering products by category across the platform. The category name must be unique across the entire platform to ensure consistent categorization and avoid confusion among users.

Validation requirements include a minimum length of 2 characters and a maximum length of 50 characters. The name should only contain alphanumeric characters and spaces, with no special characters to ensure clean URL generation and avoid potential security issues during display.

description.description:
Optional description for the product category, providing additional context about the category's purpose, target customers, or product range. This description helps improve the user experience by giving customers more information about why certain products are categorized together. It can also aid in better SEO for product category pages.

The description should not exceed 500 characters to maintain readability and prevent overwhelming users with excessive information. While not required for the API operation, providing a meaningful description enhances the browsing experience and helps with category discovery.

parentCategoryId.description:
Optional ID reference to the parent category, used to establish hierarchical category structures within the product catalog. This option allows administrators to create nested category structures that help organize products more effectively and provide a better browsing experience for customers.

The parentCategoryId must reference an existing category's ID from the shopping_mall_product_categories table. If provided, it creates a parent-child relationship where this category becomes a subcategory under the specified parent. If omitted, the category becomes a top-level category.

IShoppingMallProductSpec.IRequest.description:
Filtering and pagination parameters for product spec retrieval. This request type supports efficient filtering by attributes and sorting with pagination to allow precise specification retrieval across catalog data. The parameters are designed to match standard pagination patterns while aligning with the Product Specs database structure and user requirements for product specification browsing.

The request includes standard pagination parameters (page and limit) with sensible defaults, sorting controls (sort_by and order) to allow organization by multiple fields, and filtering capabilities to narrow down results based on product specification characteristics. All parameters follow established API patterns that are consistent with the rest of the shopping mall API.

page.description: Page number for paginated results. Must be a positive integer. Specifies which page of results to retrieve. Defaults to 1 if not provided, representing the first page of results.

limit.description: Number of items to return per page. Limited to 100 items per page to prevent excessive data loading and improve API performance. Defaults to 10 items per page if not provided.

oneOf.description: Field name to sort results by. Valid values include 'attribute_name', 'value', 'created_at', and 'updated_at'. If not specified, results are returned in default order (usually most recent first).
Field name to sort results by. Valid values include 'attribute_name', 'value', 'created_at', and 'updated_at'. If not specified, results are returned in default order (usually most recent first).

sort_by.description: Field name to sort results by. Valid values include 'attribute_name', 'value', 'created_at', and 'updated_at'. If not specified, results are returned in default order (usually most recent first).

oneOf.description: Sorting direction. 'asc' for ascending order (A-Z, 0-9), 'desc' for descending order (Z-A, 9-0). Defaults to 'desc' if not specified, which typically shows most recent items first.

order.description: Sorting direction. 'asc' for ascending order (A-Z, 0-9), 'desc' for descending order (Z-A, 9-0). Defaults to 'desc' if not specified, which typically shows most recent items first.

product_variant_id.description:
Identifier of the product variant for which the inventory adjustment is being made. The variant must belong to the seller's catalog. This parameter is a UUID reference pointing to the shopping_mall_variant_inventories database table where the actual inventory is tracked. Each product variant has a unique identifier that corresponds to specific attributes like color, size, or style.

In the context of inventory management, this field uniquely identifies which specific product variant's stock levels are being modified. For example, a product variant representing 'T-shirt in blue color, size M' would have a distinct identifier that the system uses to update the correct inventory record.

adjustment_quantity.description:
Numeric amount by which the inventory should be adjusted. Positive values add stock to inventory, while negative values reduce stock (e.g., for damaged goods or returns).

The adjustment must ensure that the resulting inventory levels remain non-negative, which is validated by the backend before processing. This parameter directly affects the current stock count in the shopping_mall_variant_inventories table and must reflect the actual physical difference in stock.

The system enforces a logical range of -9999 to 9999 to prevent extremely large adjustments while still allowing practical inventory management operations.

reason.description:
Description of why the inventory adjustment is being made. This field should provide sufficient detail for audit purposes and to differentiate between types of adjustments (e.g., 'stock received from supplier', 'damaged goods', 'returns processed').

The reason is mandatory and must be clear and specific to allow for proper tracking of all inventory changes. It does not need to be a lengthy explanation but should be descriptive enough to understand the adjustment's purpose without referring to additional external records.

Example uses: 'Restocked from warehouse', 'Scrap inventory after damage', 'Returned merchandise processed'.

IShoppingMallInventoryAdjustment.ICreate.description: Request DTO for creating a new inventory adjustment entry for product variants. This schema contains the fields required to initiate a manual inventory adjustment, including the product variant reference, adjustment amount, and justification for the adjustment. The seller's identity is automatically linked from the authentication context, so no explicit seller ID is required in the request body.

IShoppingMallProductSpec.IUpdate.description: This DTO represents the request structure for updating product specifications within a product variant. It enables partial updates to specification details such as dimensions, materials, or other attribute values, allowing efficient modification without requiring all fields. The entity is specifically designed for seller-managed modifications of product specifications. The schema follows standardized naming conventions for product specifications to ensure consistency across the catalog, including specification name, value, unit, and display rank. This DTO supports updating all specification fields while maintaining the business rule that sellers can only modify their own product specifications. It is directly linked to the shopping_mall_product_specs database table which stores product specification details.

specificationName.description:
The human-readable name of the specification (e.g., 'Material', 'Dimension', 'Color'). Represents the category or attribute being specified for the product variant.

This field must match the existing specification naming conventions used throughout the system to maintain consistent categorization. The system uses this name for grouping similar specifications, so it should reflect the attribute's purpose and follow business-side naming standards (e.g., 'Material' instead of 'Type' for fabric attributes).

specificationValue.description:
The actual value or content of the specification (e.g., '120g', 'Cotton', 'Blue'). Should match the expected format for the given specification name, providing the specific data for the product attribute.

This field holds the actual data point for the specification, such as measurement values, color names, or material types. The format may vary based on the specification name - for example, numeric values for dimensions, descriptive strings for material types. All values should conform to merchant-provided data standards for consistency in the catalog.

unit.description:
The unit of measurement for quantity or dimension specifications (e.g., 'cm', 'grams', 'in'). Required only for specifications involving measurements where the unit is part of the value's meaning.

Units are used when numerical specifications require context about the measurement type. This field can be included alongside specificationValue for measurements, making the data more meaningful. Example: specificationName 'Length', specificationValue '120', unit 'cm'. This allows the system to accurately display '120 cm' to customers.

rank.description:
The numerical position for sorting specifications within the product variant. Lower numbers appear first, higher numbers last. Specifies the display order of specifications in the catalog, with changes taking immediate effect.

This field controls the ordering of specifications in the catalog display. When updated, the system immediately refreshes the product view to reflect the new sort order. The rank must be a positive integer value, with lower numbers displayed before higher numbers in the product specifications listing.

IShoppingMallInventoryAdjustment.IReques.description: Filter parameters and pagination settings for retrieving inventory adjustment records. These parameters allow sellers to search and filter their inventory adjustments by various criteria including date ranges, product variants, adjustment types, and statuses. The request supports pagination to handle potentially large datasets efficiently.

productVariantId.description: ID of the product variant to filter inventory adjustments by. Only adjustments related to this specific product variant will be returned.

oneOf.description: Type of adjustment to filter by. Possible values include 'manual', 'system', and 'reconciled'. The adjustment type provides context about how the adjustment was created.

IShoppingMallOrder.ISummary.description: Summary representation of a shopping mall order for list views and embedded contexts. This light-weight DTO provides essential order information without including detailed compositions or sensitive data, optimized for performance in list rendering where each item needs to load quickly. The summary view excludes order items and payment details while maintaining critical context for users to identify and understand orders at a glance. This matches the pagination response structure required by the /shoppingMall/customer/orders, /shoppingMall/seller/orders, and /shoppingMall/admin/orders API paths.

id.description:
Unique system identifier for the order within the database. This is a globally unique identifier that should be stored as a UUID format string. The id is automatically generated when the order is created and never changes throughout the order's lifecycle. This identifier is used for database references and order lookup operations but is not visible to customers in UIs.

This field strictly follows the standard uuid format as defined by RFC 4122, which allows for consistent representation across all system components and integration points.

orderCode.description:
Human-readable business identifier for the order, used for reference across systems. This code follows a specific format that includes a year prefix, sequence number, and optional suffixes, making it easily identifiable in user interfaces and external systems. Orders are uniquely identifiable by this code across all platforms, allowing for cross-system tracking without requiring database queries.

The orderCode field is a public-facing identifier that may be exposed to customers, sellers, and administrators for order lookups and reference. It is generated as a unique string to prevent collisions in business operations.

oneOf.description:
Current state of the order within the shopping process. This field indicates the progress of the order through the fulfillment workflow, from initial placement through to completion or cancellation.

The defined statuses reflect the business process flow: 'pending' for new orders waiting for payment, 'processing' for orders being prepared for shipment, 'completed' for successfully delivered orders, 'canceled' for orders that were removed before processing, 'refunded' for orders that were completed but then returned to a customer, and 'failed' for orders that encountered technical issues during creation.

System transitions between these states are governed by the underlying business logic and should match the exact status strings specified here.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp of when the order was first created. This field represents the exact date and time when the order was initially submitted by the customer, formatted according to ISO 8601 standards.

The createdAt timestamp is a critical audit trail element that helps track order volume throughout different time periods, identify seasonal patterns in shopping behavior, and resolve time-sensitive issues with specific orders.

Note that updates to order status do not modify this timestamp; it remains fixed throughout the order's lifecycle.

totalPrice.description:
Total monetary value of the order excluding tax and discounts. This value represents the sum of all product prices in the order before tax, shipping, and any promotional discounts are applied.

The total price is presented as a decimal value (e.g., 49.99) where the decimal represents cents (hundredths of a currency unit). This allows for precise financial tracking without floating-point precision errors.

For display to users, this price should be formatted according to the customer's language and currency preferences, but the raw numerical value represents the base product cost.

customer.description:
Summary information about the customer who placed this order. This is a complete reference to the customer's profile that includes only essential details visible in the order context without exposing sensitive information.

The customer summary includes the customer's display name, email address (or anonymized version), and primary contact information, but does not include payment details, order history, or other sensitive fields. This allows for proper attribution of the order to the correct customer without exposing personal information.

The summary format is consistent with the IShoppingMallCustomer.ISummary type used throughout the application for customer reference.

seller.description:
Summary information about the seller responsible for this order. This is a complete reference to the seller's profile that includes only essential details visible in the order context.

The seller summary includes the seller's business name, display name for the marketplace, and primary verification status, but does not include transaction details, inventory information, or other sensitive business data. This allows for proper attribution of orders to the correct seller without revealing operational details.

The summary format is consistent with the IShoppingMallSeller.ISummary type used throughout the application for seller reference.

IShoppingMallProductReview.description:
Product review entity that represents customer feedback on a specific product. This review includes the rating, comment, product reference, and timestamp information necessary to display and manage customer reviews on the shopping platform.

The review is created by authenticated customers through the POST /shoppingMall/customer/products/{productCode}/reviews endpoint and retrieved via the GET /shoppingMall/customer/reviews/{reviewCode endpoint, ensuring proper authentication and authorization.

It provides all necessary information for displaying review content on product pages, including proper attribution to customers, product relationships, and temporal information to support sorting and filtering by creation time.

reviewCode.description:
Unique business identifier for the product review, which serves as the primary key for lookup in the shopping_mall_product_reviews table. This code is created by the system and follows the pattern REV-YYYYMMDD-NNNN where NNNN is a unique numeric sequence for each day. The reviewCode uniquely identifies each review within the system and is used as the path parameter in the GET /shoppingMall/customer/reviews/{reviewCode endpoint.

It's generated during review creation and cannot be modified after creation to ensure data integrity and consistent identification. This identifier is critical for the review system's architecture and enables efficient data retrieval.

rating.description:
Product rating given by the customer, representing quality and satisfaction on a numerical scale typically ranging from 1 to 5 stars. The rating is stored as a number with a minimum value of 1 and maximum value of 5.

This rating is calculated as a star scale in the user interface, where 1 is the lowest rating (unsatisfied) and 5 is the highest (excellent). The system validates that ratings are within this range during creation and prevents the creation of reviews with invalid ratings.

Rating values directly influence product average ratings and customer purchasing decisions, making accurate rating storage critical for business analytics and customer experience.

comment.description:
Customer's written feedback and evaluation about the product, including both positive and negative aspects. The comment must have a minimum length of 10 characters and is validated for length and content before being stored.

The comment field contains the actual user-generated text that appears on the product page, providing potential customers with detailed insights about their experience with the product. The system implements content moderation to filter out language that violates community guidelines.

Comments are critical social proof elements that significantly impact conversion rates and customer trust in the product.

product.description:
Reference to the product being reviewed, which is used to link the review to a specific product entity and provide context. This field establishes a foreign key relationship to the product entity, allowing the system to fetch product details along with review content.

The product is represented as a summary object (IShoppingMallProduct.ISummary) for efficient data retrieval in API responses. This relationship is a belongs-to association (reference relation) that uses the .ISummary pattern to provide context without circular references.

This relationship enables complete product-review context for display, sorting, and filtering operations on the frontend.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the review was created, formatted as an ISO 8601 date-time string (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ). This timestamp is automatically generated by the system and cannot be modified after review creation.

The created_at field serves as an immutable record of when the review was posted, providing historical tracking and ordering capabilities. It's used in pagination and sorting of reviews by creation time, which is critical for displaying recent reviews first.

This timestamp is used in sorting, filtering, and analytics to provide timely and relevant product feedback to potential customers.

customer.description:
Reference to the customer who left the review, which is used to attribute the review to the correct user account. This field establishes a foreign key relationship to the customer entity, allowing the system to fetch customer details along with review content.

The customer is represented as a summary object (IShoppingMallCustomer.ISummary) for efficient data retrieval in API responses. This relationship is a belongs-to association that uses the .ISummary pattern to provide context without circular references.

Customer attribution is required for the review system to properly identify and display review authors, which is critical for trust and credibility on product pages.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the order in UUID format.

This field is automatically generated and cannot be modified after order creation.
The identifier uses the standard UUID v4 format for uniqueness across the system.

This field is used for all order-related queries, updates, and deletions.
It is a required field for all order record references.

customer.description:
Reference to the customer who placed the order.

This is a summary of the customer information, sufficient for display and context.
No password or sensitive information is included.

The customer reference is mandatory and represents the identity of the ordering user.
All customer-related operations are authenticated with this identity.

seller.description:
Reference to the seller that the order is associated with.

This summary shows enough information about the seller to identify them in the order context.

The seller may be a business entity or organization that is selling products on the platform.
This field is mandatory as every order must be associated with at least one seller.

oneOf.description:
Current status of the order.

Valid status values: 'pending' (order created but payment not completed), 'processing' (order being prepared), 'shipped' (order has been dispatched), 'delivered' (order has been received), 'cancelled' (order has been stopped).

The status field is monitored by customers and sellers through the platform.
Changes to status are logged for audit purposes.

The transition path starts at 'pending' and moves sequentially through the other states.
