orderDate.description:
Timestamp when the order was created.

Recorded in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSZ).

This timestamp is automatically set when the order is created by the system.
It serves as the reference point for all order metrics, fulfillment timelines, and customer support inquiries.

The orderDate field cannot be modified after creation and is used to determine the age of the order.

totalPrice.description:
Total price of the order including all items and applicable taxes.

Calculated automatically based on product prices, selected items, and any applicable discounts.
The amount is represented as a decimal number with up to 2 decimal places for currency precision.

This field is used for financial tracking, payment processing, and customer billing.
It will include the final amount that the customer pays.

items.description:
List of items ordered along with their quantities and details.

Each item includes product information, price at the time of order, and variant details.

Items are created as a composition to the order, meaning they are created together with the order.
The entire items array represents the complete product selection for this order.

This composition relationship is direct and necessary to understand the order's contents.

IShoppingMallOrder.description:
Main entity representing a shopping order in the platform.

This schema includes all essential information about an order including the customer who placed it, the seller to fulfill it, the current order status, creation timestamp, total price, and the ordered items.

The order entity is the core business unit for transaction processing, inventory allocation, and customer delivery management.
A complete order contains all necessary information for fulfillment, billing, and customer communication.

This schema does not include sensitive payment details, which are handled in a separate payment component.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the cancellation record in the database system. This is a system-generated UUID that serves as the primary key.

The ID is immutable once created, cannot be changed, and represents the specific cancellation event across the system. It is required for all operations interacting with this cancellation, such as updates and deletions.

This ID follows the standard UUID 4 format and is unique across the entire shopping_mall_order_cancellations table without any duplicates.

orderCode.description:
Business identifier code of the order being cancelled. This is the same orderCode used in the main order management endpoints.

The orderCode is a globally unique string identifier for the order in the shopping_mall_orders table, created during order creation and verified to be unique via the database's @@unique([code]) constraint.

This field is used in the path parameter for all cancellation operations and must match a valid order's code in the order system. It is not an internal ID but a human-readable business code for external reference.

cancellationId.description:
Unique identifier specifically for the cancellation request within the order. This is a system-generated UUID that is uniquely paired with a specific order.

Unlike orderCode, this ID is generated exclusively for the cancellation request and is used in the path parameter for cancellation-specific operations. It follows the UUID format to ensure uniqueness and reliability.

Cancels that have the same orderCode value can have different cancellationId values, allowing multiple cancellation requests for a single order.

reason.description:
Reason provided by the customer or administrator for initiating the cancellation. This field contains the specific explanation given by the user for why the order is being cancelled.

The reason is validated to be at least 1 character long to prevent empty cancellation requests. It may include details about issues with the order, customer preferences, or business reasons for cancellation.

This information is used in reports, customer service communications, and system logs to understand cancellation patterns and improve customer satisfaction.

status.description:
Current status of the cancellation request within the process. This field represents the state of the cancellation in the workflow.

The status can be one of four values: 
- 'pending': Cancellation request is under review
- 'approved': Cancellation has been approved
- 'rejected': Cancellation request has been disapproved
- 'processed': Cancellation has been completed and the order is cancelled

This state transition is strictly managed by the system, with each status change recorded in the cancellation history for audit purposes.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when the cancellation request was first created in the system. This is the official starting point for the cancellation request.

The timestamp is captured at the moment the request is submitted and serves as the reference point for calculating wait times, response times, and process efficiency metrics.

This field cannot be modified after creation, as it represents the historical moment the request entered the system.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp when the cancellation request was last updated by a user or the system. This indicates the most recent time changes were made to the cancellation.

The update timestamp captures both manual changes made by staff and automatic status changes made by the system (such as when a cancellation is automatically 'processed' after a certain period).

This field may show the time of status changes, reason updates, or approver changes.

approverId.description:
Identifier of the user who approved or rejected the cancellation request. This field references the authenticated user who made the status change.

The approverId is populated with the user or administrator's ID when the cancellation status is updated. This could be the customer who initiated the cancellation (for self-update) or an administrator for official actions.

This field helps trace approval workflows and maintain accountability for cancellation decisions.

IShoppingMallOrderCancellation.description:
Order cancellation request record representing a customer-initiated or administrator-managed request to cancel an order. This serves as the main entity type for cancellation records in the system.

This entity contains all the relevant details about a specific cancellation request that has been submitted within the system. The cancellation request is tied to an order and follows the order's lifecycle, allowing customers to manage their order cancellation requests.

The system requires all these fields to maintain complete cancellation records, support status tracking, and enable audit trails. This type is used in the main response body for cancellation operations throughout the API. The cancellation status must be one of the allowed enum values to maintain consistent state management.

IShoppingMallProductCategory.IUpdate.description: Product category update DTO for the shopping platform. This schema defines all fields that can be updated for product categories, including name, hierarchical position, visibility, sorting order, and detailed descriptions. Each field has been carefully documented to provide developers with complete business context and usage instructions.

name.description: Category name to update. This field can be modified to change the category's display name in the product catalog. The name must be unique across all categories and visible to users in search results. The maximum length is 255 characters for optimal display across all platforms.

parentCategoryCode.description:
Parent category code that defines the hierarchical relationship. This can be used to move this category under a different category in the hierarchy. If this field is set to 'null', the category will become a top-level category.

The parent category must exist in the system and should be a valid code from the 'shopping_mall_product_categories' table. Setting this to an invalid code will result in a validation error.

isVisible.description:
Visibility status of the category. When set to 'true', the category will be visible to users in the catalog and participate in product discovery. When set to 'false', the category will be hidden from public view but will still be usable for internal organization and reference.

The visibility status affects whether the category appears in navigation menus, search results, and on product detail pages. Changing this status requires administrative approval for high-impact changes.

sortIndex.description:
Position of the category in the display order. Lower values appear higher in category listings, while higher values appear lower. This index is used to sort categories in product browsing interfaces and must be unique within its level of hierarchy.

The sort index can be used for manual ordering of categories beyond automatic alphabetical or date-based sorting. Values can be negative or positive, but must be whole numbers without decimal places.

description.description:
Detailed description of the product category, explaining its purpose, typical products included, and usage scenarios. This description is used for SEO optimization and customer guidance in shopping experiences, helping users understand the category's relevance to their needs.

The description should be concise yet informative, providing context about what products are typically included in this category. For example: 'This category includes all electronic devices sold through our platform, including smartphones, laptops, and accessories.'

It is visible to users on product category pages and in search results, so it should be optimized for clarity and discovery.

IShoppingMallProductReview.ISummary.description:
Minimal representation of a product review for list views and summaries, containing only essential fields for quick user display without excessive data.

This summary includes the review ID, customer name and avatar for context, average rating, and a brief visible comment snippet. It avoids detailed information and sensitive data to optimize list performance and privacy while maintaining meaningful user feedback context.

Uses customer summary for context without full profile, and limits comment detail to provide a preview for quick scanning.

id.description: Unique identifier for the review entry. Used as the primary key in the database and for reference in the system. Matches PRISMA schema field 'id' with UUID format.

rating.description: Numeric rating given by the customer for the product. Valid values range from 1 to 5 (stars), with 5 being the highest rating. Corresponds to database field 'rating' in the ProductReview model.

customer.description: Summary information of the customer who wrote the review. Provides context about the reviewer without loading their full profile. This reference uses the customer's summary object, ensuring minimal data transfer while maintaining user context for social proof purposes.

commentPreview.description: Shortened version of the full review comment, typically the first 50-100 characters. This preview gives a quick glimpse of the review content without overwhelming the list view. The full comment is not included in summaries to maximize performance.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the review was created. Indicates the review's age and freshness, used for sorting and filtering. Matches the database timestamp field 'created_at' with ISO 8601 format.

IShoppingMallInventoryAdjustment.ISummar.description:
Summary representation of inventory adjustment records optimized for display in seller inventory management interfaces. Includes essential fields for quick reference without full entity details, allowing for efficient pagination and listing of adjustment history. This type is used in paginated responses for the inventory adjustment endpoint, excluding detailed composition data to maintain performance.

Used as part of the page response to provide a concise view of each adjustment record, allowing sellers to quickly scan through their inventory adjustment history. The summary form includes only fields that are relevant for listing views, while more detailed information can be retrieved via separate requests for specific adjustment records.

The schema is structured to match the response requirements for the inventory adjustment index endpoint, following the IPage container pattern where each item is an instance of this summary type.

This schema includes status and adjustment type fields which were previously missing, providing essential business context for inventory management operations.

The status field tracks the processing state of the inventory adjustment, while the adjustment_type field provides context about how the adjustment was created (manual, system-generated, or reconciled). These additions ensure the schema accurately represents all business requirements for adjustment records.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the inventory adjustment record. Used as the primary key in the database and to reference this specific adjustment instance. Must be in UUID format for consistency across the platform and to ensure uniqueness.

Generated automatically by the system during adjustment creation, and never provided by the client. Essential for any operations requiring precise identification of a specific adjustment record, such as fetching full details or making modifications.

previous_quantity.description:
The stock quantity before the adjustment was applied. This value represents the inventory level at the time the adjustment request was submitted, serving as a reference point for the adjustment's impact.

Always a non-negative integer. Required to calculate the adjustment delta and to provide transparency in inventory changes. Used in both the inventory adjustment UI and audit logs to show the inventory state before the change.

adjusted_quantity.description:
The stock quantity after the adjustment was applied. Represents the new inventory level reflecting the adjustment made, showing the current stock count for the product variant.

Always a non-negative integer. This value is critical for inventory management as it directly affects stock availability calculations. Also used to validate against the previous quantity to prevent negative inventory states.

product_variant.description:
Reference to the product variant whose inventory was adjusted. Provides key details of the product variant without including the full product details, optimizing for performance in listing scenarios.

The reference includes the product variant ID, name, and SKU information for quick identification. This is a BELONGS-TO relation transformed into a summary object, as per the DTO design patterns.

adjustment_reason.description:
Reason provided by the seller for the inventory adjustment. Explains the business context for the inventory change, such as 'manual stock count correction' or 'damaged goods adjustment'.

Must be a human-readable text description of the adjustment purpose. A required field for audit purposes, providing context for the change in inventory that might not be obvious from the quantity differences alone.

oneOf.description: Status of the adjustment to indicate processing state. The 'pending' status represents an adjustment that has been submitted but not yet processed.
Status of the adjustment to indicate processing state. The 'approved' status represents a valid adjustment that has been processed successfully.
Status of the adjustment to indicate processing state. The 'rejected' status represents an adjustment that has been reviewed and declined.

status.description:
Status of the inventory adjustment processing. Indicates the current state of the adjustment and whether it's been approved or rejected by the system or administrators.

The status field tracks the progression of adjustments through the system. Used for filtering adjustment history and determining which adjustments require attention.

oneOf.description: Type of adjustment to indicate origin. The 'manual' type represents adjustments created by sellers directly.
Type of adjustment to indicate origin. The 'system' type represents automatic adjustments generated by background processes.
Type of adjustment to indicate origin. The 'reconciled' type represents adjustments created during inventory reconciliation processes.

adjustment_type.description:
Type of inventory adjustment creation. Indicates how the adjustment was created (manually by seller, automatically by the system, or during reconciliation).

This distinction is critical for inventory audit trails. Manual adjustments require seller confirmation, system adjustments are automated, and reconciled adjustments are part of inventory balancing processes.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the inventory adjustment record was created. Shows the exact date and time the adjustment was logged in the system.

Always a valid ISO 8601 timestamp. Used for sorting in lists, determining the order of adjustments, and identifying the most recent inventory changes. Required for any chronological display of adjustment history.

IShoppingMallVariantInventory.ICreate.description: Creates a new inventory adjustment record for specific product variants. Seller identity is automatically included from authentication context (seller_id), so not required in request body. Represents the 'Manual Stock Adjustment' user scenario, enabling sellers to correct inventory counts while maintaining audit trails for all modifications. The schema excludes all system-managed fields and authentication context fields per security requirements.

IShoppingMallOrderSnapshot.description:
Represents a historical snapshot of an order at a specific point in time, capturing the state of the order including its status, associated products, and fulfillment details at the moment the snapshot was taken.

This snapshot includes the full context of the order at that specific moment, allowing for accurate historical tracking of order status changes, product selections, and fulfillment progress. The snapshot is designed to provide a clear audit trail of the order's lifecycle and should be used in order history, status change tracking, and historical reporting.

Key considerations include:
- The snapshot is tied to a specific order (via orderCode) and has its own unique identifier
- It contains the full product details included in the order at the time of the snapshot
- Status reflects the order's state at the moment the snapshot was created
- Timestamps capture the exact moments of snapshot creation and updates for audit purposes
- All timestamp fields (createdAt, updatedAt) follow ISO 8601 format to ensure global time standardization

id.description: Unique identifier for the snapshot record, automatically generated by the system. This is different from the order's identifier and is used specifically for tracking snapshots.

orderCode.description: The global business identifier code of the parent order. This is the same order code used in the endpoint path and represents the original order that the snapshot belongs to. Unlike the snapshot's internal id, this code is business-readable and maintained across the system.

status.description: Current status of the order at the moment the snapshot was created. Represents the order's state in the business workflow (e.g., 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered', 'cancelled') and reflects the exact status held at the snapshot time.

products.description: List of products included in the order at the time this snapshot was taken. Each item contains a summary version of the product to keep the snapshot lightweight while providing sufficient detail for reporting and historical review. Note that historical snapshots may include products that have been removed from the current order.

IShoppingMallVariantInventory.IUpdate.description:
Request DTO for updating variant inventory quantity. Allows sellers to adjust stock levels for product variants, updating the real inventory records in the database. The update validates that the quantity change is non-negative and within business constraints, and triggers any configured low stock alerts if the new quantity falls below the alert threshold. Note: Only quantity is updateable - all other inventory fields like variant_id and product_id are immutable as they're considered identity fields.

The schema represents the specific information needed to change the quantity of a product variant's stock in the shopping mall platform's inventory system. This quantity change directly affects product availability and triggers low stock alerts when crossing configured thresholds.

Validation ensures that quantity is a non-negative integer, preventing invalid inventory adjustments that could lead to system errors or inaccurate stock visibility. The quantity field must be provided as an integer without decimal points.

This DTO is exclusively used in the PUT /shoppingMall/seller/variant/inventories/{inventoryId operation for updating inventory quantities, where the path parameter {inventoryId specifies which inventory record to modify and the request body provides the new quantity value.

quantity.description: New inventory quantity value for the product variant. Must be a non-negative integer. This value is validated against business constraints (e.g., not exceeding inventory capacity) and applied to the database inventory record. The quantity directly affects product availability and low stock alert triggers.

IShoppingMallOrderCancellation.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of order cancellation requests for customer view. This type provides essential cancellation details in a compact format suitable for list views without requiring additional API calls. The summary includes the cancellation's essential metadata and status for quick user reference, while excluding detailed refund information that would be displayed in a separate endpoint. This implementation follows the atomic operation principle by providing all necessary information in a single response for list display.

The schema directly maps to the OrderCancellation database table, with all properties being optional fields that exist in the database schema (except for the required fields). Each property serves a specific purpose in the shopping system, with status and refund status indicating the current processing state of the cancellation. This summary view ensures performance efficiency and prevents N+1 query problems when displaying cancellation lists.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the cancellation request. This is the primary key in the database and guarantees uniqueness across all cancellation records. Must match the UUID format as defined by the database schema, and is used to reference the specific cancellation when performing additional operations like viewing details or managing the cancellation state.

This field is required for all summary views as it identifies individual cancellation entries in the list and allows clients to reference specific requests without additional database queries. The UUID format ensures compatibility with database indexing and efficient lookups.

orderCode.description:
Order code associated with the cancellation request. Represents the unique identifier of the parent order that the cancellation is applied to. This is a foreign key referencing the orders table.

This field is crucial for the customer to understand which order the cancellation request pertains to, and follows the same naming convention as the path parameter used in the API endpoint ("/orders/{orderCode}"). It enables quick mapping between the cancellation record and its related order without additional API calls.

reason.description:
Human-readable reason for the cancellation request. Captures the customer's stated reason when initiating cancellation, such as 'change of mind', 'product not as described', or 'shipping delay'.

This field provides business context for the cancellation, enabling quick customer service resolution if additional clarification is needed. The field should be concise but descriptive, allowing the customer to understand why they canceled the order without requiring additional API calls to retrieve details.

status.description:
Current status of the cancellation request. Represents the processing state of the request, such as 'pending', 'approved', 'rejected', or 'completed'.

This status field is critical for the customer to understand the current state of their cancellation request. The available values are strictly limited to the ones defined in the business rules, ensuring consistent client-side behavior. This field's value directly reflects the internal processing state as managed in the system.

refundStatus.description:
Status of the associated refund request. Indicates the processing state of the refund, such as 'pending', 'processed', 'failed', or 'refunded'.

This field provides immediate feedback on the refund process, which is a critical part of the cancellation workflow. The status must correspond to the status field in the refund system, enabling customers to understand when they'll receive their funds back. This field's purpose is solely to provide a quick status indicator for the refund process.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when the cancellation request was submitted. Records the exact date and time (in UTC) when the customer initiated the cancellation request, formatted in ISO 8601 standard.

This field is important for historical tracking and for determining the age of the cancellation request. It follows the same date-time format used throughout the application, ensuring consistent temporal data display. Clients can use this timestamp to sort cancellation requests and display them chronologically.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the variant inventory record. This is an immutable system-generated ID used to uniquely identify inventory entries in the database.

The ID follows UUID v4 format to ensure global uniqueness and security. It's automatically generated when the inventory record is created and never changes. Clients should never attempt to set or modify this value.

This ID serves as the primary key for inventory records and is used in all database queries, API endpoints, and audit logs for inventory management operations.

quantity.description:
Current stock quantity for the product variant. Represents the number of units available in the current inventory system.

This value is always a non-negative integer (0 or higher). A value of 0 indicates the variant is out of stock. The quantity is updated in real-time as orders are placed and inventory is adjusted.

This field is critical for sellers managing product listings as it directly affects visibility in the shopping interface and customer purchase decisions.

variant.description:
The product variant being tracked in inventory.

This is a relationship to the specific product variant that the inventory record represents. It contains essential details about the variant without full composition data (e.g., name, color, size).

This reference allows sellers to quickly identify which product variant is affected by the inventory status. It's transformed from the raw variant_id for complete context in listing views.

product.description:
The parent product to which the variant belongs.

This shows the main product the variant is part of (e.g., 'Smartphone' for a variant like 'Smartphone - Blue - 128GB'). It provides context about the product category and main characteristics.

The product reference includes minimal details necessary for listing view, but excludes detailed variant information which is covered separately by the variant reference.

IShoppingMallVariantInventories.ISummary.description:
Product variant inventory summary used for listing inventory data in seller's dashboard. This type provides essential visibility into stock levels across product variants while minimizing data transfer.

It's designed for performance in list views, containing only fields necessary to quickly assess inventory health without requiring full product details. Includes references to the variant and parent product for context.

This summary type is used in the '/shoppingMall/seller/variant/inventories' endpoint response to provide efficient views of variant inventory records for sellers.

IShoppingMallProductImage.description: Main product image entity in the shopping mall platform, representing a single image file associated with a product. This entity stores the image metadata used for catalog display and product page presentation. The schema reflects the ShoppingMallProductImage database table structure and includes all necessary fields for public product listings. Fields are organized to provide necessary content for display purposes while maintaining efficient data transfer.

id.description: Unique identifier for the product image record in the database. Used as the primary key to reference the image within the system and for API operations. This UUID is generated at record creation and never changes, ensuring consistent identification across all platform interactions.

product.description: Product the image belongs to. This reference provides the complete product information without requiring additional API calls to fetch the product details. Used for context in image display operations where full product information is needed.

dimensions.description: Image dimensions in the format 'width x height' (e.g., '1920x1080'). This field is used for responsive design and layout optimization across different device sizes. The dimensions directly impact how images appear on product pages and are crucial for maintaining visual consistency in the platform's user interface.

position.description: Display order position of the image among all images for the product. Lower position numbers appear first in product image galleries and are considered primary images. This integer value is used to determine the sequence of images shown on product pages, with the default being 0 for the main product image.

payment_method_id.description:
Identifier of the payment method selected for this order. Must reference an existing payment method configuration from the shopping_mall_payment_methods database table.

This field must contain a valid UUID that exists in the payment methods table to ensure payment processing can proceed. The system validates the payment method is active and configured for the platform before order approval.

Payment method selection is a critical success factor for order completion, as it determines the payment gateway used and affects payment processing workflows.

IShoppingMallOrder.ICreate.description:
Order creation payload for customer orders. Contains payment reference.

The operation validates required fields including product existence in the database, minimum item quantity (≥1), valid address format with all required components, and valid payment method reference before order creation.

Customer identity is automatically populated from authenticated session context, so customer ID is not required in the request body. The order status automatically initializes as 'pending' and triggers payment processing workflows.

This schema matches the Primary Scenario 'Order Placement Process' requirement and ensures all necessary components (products, items, payment) are properly linked to the order record.

IShoppingMallReview.description:
Product reviews represent customer feedback on shopping mall items, providing social proof and influencing purchasing decisions. This schema captures detailed review data including the customer's experience, star rating, and product context, with business-identifiable codes for URL readability and performance.

The review system is designed to encourage genuine customer feedback while preventing spam through minimum content requirements. Each review is tied to a specific product and customer, with the reviewCode serving as the primary URL identifier. This structure enables the platform to dynamically update review counts and average ratings across product listings without additional database calls. The schema supports both read and write operations with appropriate validation, ensuring feedback quality while maintaining privacy through abbreviated customer information in public display.

reviewCode.description: Unique business identifier code for the review, generated upon creation using the pattern REVIEW-YYYYMMDD-NNNN. This code serves as the primary key for the review in the system, allowing efficient URL construction and database lookups without exposing internal IDs. It is immutable once generated and cannot be changed after review creation.

product.description: Reference to the product summary entity (IShoppingMallProduct.ISummary), providing complete product context without requiring additional API calls. Contains all essential product data for display, including name, category, price, and aggregated rating statistics. This reference allows direct access to product details without additional API requests for context.

customer.description: Reference to the customer summary (IShoppingMallCustomer.ISummary), showing relevant customer details without exposing sensitive account information. Includes display name, account status, and minimal identifying information for social proof context. This ensures privacy while providing context about who left the review.

content.description: The actual customer review text providing product experience details. Must be at least 20 characters to prevent spam, and up to 1000 characters for clarity. The field is publicly displayed and should contain specific product feedback rather than generic phrases, directly impacting user trust in the product. Content must be in clear, readable language providing specific insights about the product experience.

rating.description: Customer's star rating on a scale of 1-5. Values are integers, not floats or percentages, to maintain consistent user interface display. Rating of 1 indicates significant dissatisfaction, while 5 indicates excellent satisfaction, with an average calculated for product listings. This field is mandatory and directly affects product visibility and ranking.

amount.description:
Refund amount to be processed, must be positive and not exceed the original order amount. Should be specified to two decimal places (such as 29.99) for monetary values.

The amount must be greater than 0.01 to avoid processing issues, and cannot exceed the original order value. This field is required for all refund requests to ensure proper financial processing.

This is the total amount the system will process for the refund, which may include partial refunds for certain order items and their related payment amounts.

reason.description:
Reason for the refund request provided by the user, describing the issue or specific request.

This field must be between 1-255 characters, providing enough detail to understand the reason for the refund without being overly verbose. Example: 'Product arrived damaged' or 'No longer needed after delivery'.

The reason helps in processing the refund request appropriately and provides documentation for customer service and financial auditing purposes.

IShoppingMallOrderRefund.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for initiating an order refund. This DTO includes the essential refund amount and reason required for processing the refund request, without any actor-specific or system-managed fields.

Authorization for refunds is handled through the authenticated actor context (customer/seller), so no user_id fields are included. The order reference is provided via the path parameter as 'orderCode' instead of including it in the request body.

This schema follows the atomic operation principle - all required information for a complete refund request is provided in a single API call without needing additional API requests for related data.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the inventory adjustment record, generated as UUID when the adjustment is created.

This ID serves as the primary key for the adjustment record in the database and is used in all API operations related to this adjustment. The value should be globally unique across all inventory adjustments.

productVariant.description:
Reference to the specific product variant affected by this adjustment.

This field links the adjustment to a product variant in the shopping_mall_variant_inventories table, representing the product variant whose inventory is being modified. The value must exist as a valid product variant ID in the system.

adjustment_quantity.description:
The numerical value of the inventory adjustment, indicating quantity change.

Positive values represent adding stock, while negative values represent subtracting stock. This value must not result in negative inventory levels after adjustment.

Example: +50 for adding 50 items to stock, -10 for removing 10 items from stock.

reason.description:
Text explanation for why the adjustment was made.

This field provides a detailed reason for the inventory adjustment, which can include reasons like 'Restocking after warehouse delivery', 'Damage in transit', or 'Seasonal clearance'. The description should be clear and actionable for inventory management.

seller.description:
Reference to the seller who initiated the adjustment.

This ID links the adjustment to a specific seller in the system, verifying ownership of the adjustment. The seller ID is automatically set from the authenticated session during creation, ensuring it corresponds to the seller account making the adjustment.

oneOf.description:
Current status of the inventory adjustment workflow.

The adjustment moves through a status workflow: PENDING (initial state, awaiting verification), APPROVED (verified and applied to inventory), or REJECTED (not approved and not applied). This status is updated through the update endpoint and visible in the detailed response.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the inventory adjustment was first created.

This timestamp records the exact time the adjustment was created in the system, used for audit purposes and order of operations. The value represents a valid UTC timestamp formatted according to ISO 8601 standards.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the inventory adjustment was last modified.

This timestamp is automatically updated whenever any field of the adjustment is changed through update operations. It reflects the most recent change to the adjustment record and is used for tracking modification history.

IShoppingMallInventoryAdjustment.description:
Inventory adjustment records that track manual inventory changes made by sellers for product variants.

These records document the inventory modification process including the product affected, the quantity change, the reason for adjustment, and the seller who initiated the change. Each adjustment creates a permanent record in the inventory adjustment history for auditing purposes.

The system enforces business rules that prevent negative inventory levels, requires detailed reason documentation, and tracks the full lifecycle of adjustments from creation to final status. The records are used in reconciliation processes and provide essential data for inventory reporting and analysis.

Adjustments are created through the seller inventory adjustment API and updated by sellers or administrators using specific endpoints. The status workflow enables proper oversight and approval for inventory modifications, ensuring that all changes are properly authorized and documented.

quantity.description:
Current quantity of the product variant in the order. This field represents the number of units of the product variant that the customer has ordered.

The system validates that the new quantity does not exceed available inventory levels when updating. Quantities must be at least 1 unit.

If updating the quantity would cause inventory shortage, the API returns an error response before making the change, preventing inventory consistency issues.

IShoppingMallOrderItem.IUpdate.description:
Request DTO for updating order items within orders. Allows modification of quantity, price, and special instructions for order items while maintaining all immutable fields like order and product references.
The API validates that changes do not cause inventory inconsistencies or pricing mismatches before applying updates.

IShoppingMallOrderCancellation.IRequest.description:
Filtering parameters for order cancellation request lists, used by customers to retrieve their order cancellations with specific parameters. This request schema supports pagination, sorting, and conditional filtering to reduce data transfer and improve API efficiency for customer use cases. The schema includes standard search parameters that map to database columns for efficient query execution.

Customers use this request DTO to filter their order cancellation history based on specific criteria, allowing them to view cancellations in a paginated format. The operation integrates with the OrderCancellation table from the database schema, applying security filters to ensure customers can only access their own cancellation records. The parameters provided enable the system to build precise SQL queries for fetching the required dataset efficiently.

page.description: Page number for pagination. Starts from 1, default value is 1 if omitted. This parameter controls which subset of results to return based on the specified limit. Valid values are positive integers greater than or equal to 1.

limit.description: Number of items per page. Defaults to 10. Valid range is 1-100. This parameter determines how many cancellation items are included in each response. Higher values improve page efficiency but reduce network efficiency for large datasets.

sortBy.description: Field to sort by. Supports fields like 'created_at' or 'status'. When this parameter is omitted, the default sort is by 'created_at' in descending order. This field must match one of the sortable columns documented in the API's sorting specification.

oneOf.description: Sorting direction. Valid values are 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending). Default value is 'desc' for date-based fields. This parameter works in conjunction with 'sortBy' to control the sort order of results.

Sorting direction. Valid values are 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending). Default value is 'desc' for date-based fields. This parameter works in conjunction with 'sortBy' to control the sort order of results.

order.description: Sorting direction. Valid values are 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending). Default value is 'desc' for date-based fields. This parameter works in conjunction with 'sortBy' to control the sort order of results.

oneOf.description: Filter cancellations by status. Valid values: 'pending', 'approved', 'rejected'. When specified, only cancellations with the matching status are included in the response. This allows customers to filter their cancellation history based on current status. The field name matches the 'status' column in the shopping_mall_order_cancellations database table.

This enables customers to search for specific cancellation reasons, such as 'order error' or 'shipping delay'. The search is case-insensitive and matches against the 'reason' column in the database schema.

IShoppingMallOrderRefund.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of refund requests designed for efficient pagination and display.

Contains essential information needed for users to view and manage their refund history without exposing sensitive details.

This DTO is exclusively used for listing operations where complete entity detail is not required.

Serves as the data structure for customer and admin refund history views.

Excludes sensitive payment information and user identity data by design.

id.description:
Unique system identifier for the refund request.

Generated by the database upon creation of the refund record.

This identifier is immutable once created.

Follows UUIDv4 format as defined in RFC4122.

Used for all API reference operations and database relationships.

amount.description:
Refund amount to be processed in the transaction currency.

Must be a strictly positive decimal value with up to two decimal places.

Represents the total refund amount after any applicable processing fees have been subtracted.

Valid range: $0.01 - $999,999.99.

This field is derived from the original order value and refund terms.

status.description:
Current status of the refund request in the business workflow.

Valid status values:
- 'pending': Submission has been received but not yet processed
- 'approved': Refund has been authorized and is being processed
- 'rejected': Refund request was denied per business rules
- 'cancelled': Request was cancelled by the customer

Status transitions follow specific business rules and cannot be reversed.

Status changes automatically based on processing workflows.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when the refund request was submitted to the system.

Recorded at the exact moment of creation.

Formatted according to ISO 8601 standard.

This timestamp does not reflect processing status changes.

System-generated and immutable.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the refund record within the system. Stored as a UUID in the database to ensure global uniqueness and avoid sequential predictability. This is the primary key for the refund record and should be considered immutable once created.

The ID is used in all API operations to reference specific refund records, following standard UUID format with consistent 36-character length including hyphens.

oneOf.description:
Current state of the refund request in the processing workflow. Represents the status of the refund as it moves through the refund management lifecycle.

The status transitions follow a strict workflow: pending → either approved, rejected, or canceled. The value must be one of the predefined options and cannot be arbitrary text.

Business rules: Once a refund is rejected, it cannot be approved later. Canceled refunds are typically initiated by the customer before final processing, while rejected refunds are processed by the system with a reason provided.

amount.description:
Amount to be refunded in the transaction currency. Represents the exact monetary value that will be processed for this refund.

This amount must be greater than zero and must not exceed the original order amount. For partial refunds, the amount is less than the original order amount.

The currency is standardized as the platform's base currency (USD) for all refunds, with automatic conversion rates handled by the payment gateway.

reason.description:
Reason provided by the customer or seller for requesting the refund. Explains the context behind the refund request and helps with dispute resolution.

This field contains free-form text that describes why the refund is being requested (e.g., 'Product damaged on delivery', 'Item not as described', 'Customer changed mind'). The content should be clear and specific to help identify patterns in refund requests.

Business rule: This is required for all refund requests initiated by customers, but may be optional for seller-initiated refunds.

order.description:
Summary reference to the purchase order associated with this refund request. Provides essential details about the order without including all the order's data.

This is a BELONGS-TO relation showing which order is being refunded, using the order's summary representation. It includes the order code, customer information, and basic order status without requiring a full order retrieval.

The reference ensures proper linkback to the parent order without causing recursive relationship issues.

paymentTransaction.description:
Summary reference to the payment transaction linked to this refund. Provides essential payment details without requiring a full transaction retrieval.

This is a BELONGS-TO relation showing which payment was affected by the refund processing. It includes payment gateway details, status, and amount without requiring unnecessary payment details.

The reference ensures proper reconciliation between the refund and payment without duplicating payment data.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when the refund request was first created in the system. Recorded in ISO 8601 format with nanosecond precision.

This timestamp is automatically populated when the refund record is created and cannot be modified afterwards. It's used to determine the age of refund requests and for reporting purposes.

Business use case: This field helps identify refund requests initiated before or after specific time periods for analytics.

updatedAt.description:
Last timestamp when the refund record was updated with new status or details. Recorded in ISO 8601 format with nanosecond precision.

This timestamp updates automatically whenever the refund status changes or additional details are added. It's used to determine when the most recent changes to the refund occurred.

Business use case: This field helps identify active refund requests that require attention versus those with no recent updates.

IShoppingMallOrderRefund.description:
Represents a refund request for an order within the shopping mall platform. This entity tracks the status, amount, and processing details of refunds for both customers and sellers.

The primary purpose of this entity is to manage the refund workflow, including creation, processing, approval, rejection, and cancellation. Each refund request must be associated with a specific order and payment transaction, forming a clear audit trail.

This entity is used in refund detail GET operations and in the response body of refund creation POST operations. The schema includes all necessary fields for customer-facing display and internal processing while adhering to security requirements by omitting sensitive payment details.

It's designed to be fully self-contained for retrieval, eliminating the need for additional API calls to fetch related order and payment details.

product_id.description:
Product identifier used to filter reviews for specific products.

This parameter accepts UUID-formatted values corresponding to shopping_mall_products table records. When included, limits search results to reviews specifically associated with the specified product.

The parameter supports exact match filtering, allowing customers to view all reviews for a particular product item.

Example usage: ?product_id=prod-123456

rating.description:
Rating value to filter reviews by star rating.

Accepts numeric values between 1 (1 star) and 5 (5 stars). When used, limits search results to reviews matching the specified star rating.

The parameter supports filtering with exact ratings (e.g., 4.0) and can be combined with other filters for granular search results.

Example usage: ?rating=4

page.description:
Page number for pagination.

Accepts numeric values starting from 1. Defaults to 1 if not specified.

Controls which page of results is returned when paginating large result sets.

Example usage: ?page=3

limit.description:
Number of results per page.

Accepts integer values between 1-100. Defaults to 20 for standard search operations.

Determines how many items appear in each page of results for paginated responses.

Example usage: ?limit=50

oneOf.description:
Field to sort results by.

Accepts fields such as 'created_at', 'rating', or 'product_id'. Defaults to 'created_at' if not specified.

Specifies the column by which search results should be ordered.

Example usage: ?sort_by=rating

IShoppingMallReview.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for searching product reviews, supporting filtering by product, rating, pagination, and sorting.

This data structure implements search capabilities for customer review discovery across the shopping platform. It enables filtering for specific product reviews, customer review history, and rating-based searches, with standard pagination parameters for efficient browsing.

The implementation follows database schema constraints where applicable (e.g., product_id and user_id use UUID references). All parameters are optional to allow flexible search combinations, with defaults set for common use cases.

This DTO was designed for the /shoppingMall/reviews and /shoppingMall/customer/reviews/search endpoints based on the provided API operation specifications.

order_id.description: Unique identifier of the order requiring a refund. This order must exist and belong to the authenticated customer. The system validates ownership against the shopping_mall_orders table before creating a refund request.

reason.description: Reason provided by the customer for requesting a refund. This field captures the customer's explanation for why they believe a refund is warranted, including any relevant details about the product or service.

amount_requested.description: The monetary amount requested for the refund, expressed in the default currency of the system. This amount must match the payment amount or a portion of it as specified by the refund policy. The system validates against the payment transaction's value before creation.

supporting_documentation.description: Reference URL to any supporting documentation provided by the customer for the refund request. This can include images, receipts, correspondence, or other evidence that supports the refund claim. The URL should be accessible for review by support staff.

IShoppingMallRefundRequest.ICreate.description: Request DTO for creating a new refund request. This schema captures all information required from a customer to submit a refund request. The customer must own the order and the order must be eligible for a refund (completed with successful payment) before the request can be created. The system automatically sets the initial status to 'pending' and creates a unique tracking identifier for the request.

IShoppingMallPaymentTransaction.ISummary.description:
Payment transaction summary representation designed for efficient display in customer order history and administrative transaction listings. This DTO provides the essential information required for users to track payment status without revealing sensitive details such as payment token or transaction amounts in full detail.

This summary type establishes critical relationships with related entities: the payment_method field links to the configured payment method details, enabling users to identify the payment channel used, while the order field provides context by connecting to the specific shopping order transaction. These relationships make it possible to trace payments back to their original orders for customer support.

The schema enforces validation through mandatory fields like amount (greater than zero) and status (one of four predefined values), ensuring data integrity. Designed for pagination and filtering operations, this DTO optimizes API response size by excluding non-essential fields like payment processor details, transaction IDs, and full customer information, maintaining both performance and security compliance in transaction history APIs.

id.description: Unique identifier for the payment transaction within the system. This ID is used to reference this specific transaction in all related operations and should not be reused for other transactions. The ID follows UUIDv4 standards, ensuring global uniqueness and security within the payment system.

amount.description: Amount being paid or refunded for this transaction, expressed in the platform's default currency (usually USD) with two decimal places. Represents the numeric value of payment in the smallest currency unit (e.g., cents), but displayed as dollars for user interfaces. All amounts must be greater than zero, with values calculated by summing item prices and any applicable taxes or fees.

oneOf.description: Payment processing has started but is not completed
Payment has been successfully processed
Payment attempt was rejected by the payment gateway
Full payment amount has been returned to the customer

status.description: Payment status indicating current state of the transaction. Valid values include 'pending', 'completed', 'failed', and 'refunded'. This field is critical for users to understand transaction status without accessing detailed processing logs.

created_at.description: Timestamp indicating exact moment this payment transaction was initiated. Captures user's attempt to pay rather than when payment was processed. Follows ISO 8601 format (RFC 3339) for consistent time representation across all time zones.

payment_method.description: Reference to payment method used for this transaction. Includes payment type (credit card, wallet, etc.) and basic details. Represents configuration of payment channels available in the system. Excludes sensitive details like payment identifiers for display purposes.

order.description: Reference to the order this payment is associated with. Enables tracking of payment status against specific customer orders. Links payment transaction to broader shopping activity for purchase validation and customer support.

id.description:
Unique identifier for this variant inventory entry.

This ID serves as the primary key for the inventory record. It is generated by the system when the record is created and remains unchanged throughout its lifecycle.

The ID follows standard UUID version 4 format, ensuring uniqueness across the entire system.

quantity.description:
Current stock quantity of the product variant.

The quantity represents the number of items available for sale or shipping. This value is updated in real-time as sales occur and inventory adjustments are made.

This field must be non-negative and reflects the immediate availability of the variant. Quantities are updated during order processing and manual inventory adjustments.

oneOf.description:
Current availability status of the product variant.

This field reflects the current inventory state based on the quantity. 'available' means sufficient stock, 'low' indicates quantity below threshold, and 'out_of_stock' means no stock available.

The status is automatically updated based on predefined threshold values and is used to trigger low stock alerts.

Current availability status of the product variant.

This field reflects the current inventory state based on the quantity. 'available' means sufficient stock, 'low' indicates quantity below threshold, and 'out_of_stock' means no stock available.

The status is automatically updated based on predefined threshold values and is used to trigger low stock alerts.

This field reflects the current inventory state based on the quantity. 'available' means sufficient stock, 'low' indicates quantity below threshold, and 'out_of_stock' means no stock available.

The status is automatically updated based on predefined threshold values and is used to trigger low stock alerts.

Current availability status of the product variant.

This field reflects the current inventory state based on the quantity. 'available' means sufficient stock, 'low' indicates quantity below threshold, and 'out_of_stock' means no stock available.

The status is automatically updated based on predefined threshold values and is used to trigger low stock alerts.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when this inventory record was first created.

This timestamp represents the moment the record entered the system. It is used for historical tracking and audit trails.

The value is fixed at the time of record creation and cannot be modified, providing a reliable reference for when the inventory state was established.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp when this inventory record was last modified.

This timestamp is updated every time the stock quantity is changed, either through sales or manual adjustments.

The value is automatically maintained by the system, reflecting the most recent activity that affected the inventory level.

IShoppingMallVariantInventory.description: Represents a specific stock level for a product variant. Tracks quantity, availability status, and update history for inventory management. Contains the complete snapshot of inventory at the time of creation or last update.

IShoppingMallOrderItem.ICreate.description:
Order item creation request DTO designed for sellers to add products to existing customer orders for fulfillment tracking.

This data transfer object represents a new item to be added to an existing order, specifically enabling sellers to reference a product variant belonging to their merchant context and specify the desired quantity. The operation ensures that only valid product variants (associated with the same merchant as the order) can be added to the order, preventing invalid additions or unauthorized product access.

The system validates that the product variant belongs to the merchant context of the order (determined by the authenticated seller's business account), and also ensures that the requested quantity does not exceed available inventory levels before creating the order item. The product variant and quantity fields are the only user-provided fields in this creation DTO, as all other order item fields are automatically populated by the system upon creation.

This DTO is used in API operations that allow sellers to modify orders (specifically POST /shoppingMall/seller/orders/{orderCode}/items), and its structure and validation rules are critical for maintaining accurate inventory tracking and order fulfillment processes in the shopping mall platform.

productVariantId.description:
Unique identifier for the product variant being added to the order. Must reference a product variant that belongs to the same merchant as the order.

The system validates that the product variant is associated with the merchant context of the order (determined by the authenticated seller's business account). Invalid if the variant belongs to a different merchant, as this would violate platform security protocols and could lead to incorrect order creation.

The product variant ID should be a UUID as defined in RFC 4122, formatted as a 32-character hexadecimal string with four hyphens separating five groups of digits (e.g., "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000"). This standard format ensures consistent identification across all systems and applications.

quantity.description:
Number of units of the product variant to be added to the order. Must be a positive integer (minimum value: 1).

The system validates that the requested quantity doesn't exceed the available inventory levels for the specified product variant. This validation prevents overbooking of inventory items and protects the seller's inventory management system's integrity.

The quantity value represents the physical quantity ordered and is used for inventory calculations, order fulfillment, and billing purposes. It must be a whole number (integer) and cannot be zero or negative.

IShoppingMallOrderRefund.IUpdate.description:
Update request DTO for order refunds. Contains only modifiable fields for updating refund status, amount, and reason. All fields are optional, allowing partial updates.

This DTO maps to the shopping_mall_order_refunds database table, where status, amount, and reason fields can be modified via partial update operations. Fields like id, order_id, and timestamps are omitted as they are system-generated or immutable.

Security validation ensures users can only modify refunds they own or that fall within their role-based permissions. All changes trigger automated email notifications to customers and are logged for audit purposes.

oneOf.description:
Current processing state of the refund request in the refund management workflow. Represents the current status value within the allowed transition path.

The status follows a strict business workflow: 'pending' → 'approved', 'rejected', or 'canceled'. This transition sequence is strictly enforced to maintain refund processing integrity and prevent invalid state changes.

Business rule: Once a refund status transitions to 'rejected', it cannot be moved back to 'approved' or 'processing' states, preserving audit trail integrity and preventing workflow violations.

Finalized status for a refund request indicating approval and processing. Marks the refund as approved for payment processing.

This is the final state in the refund workflow after verification and approval. The refund amount will be processed to the original payment method upon reaching this status.

Business rule: This state can only be reached from 'pending' status, not directly from 'rejected' or 'canceled' states.

Status indicating the refund request was declined or rejected. Represents the system's formal rejection of the refund request.

This status indicates the refund is processed as rejected, with any potential reversal of the payment being handled as a separate process.

Business rule: This status can be reached from 'pending', but once reached, the status cannot transition back to 'approved' or 'pending'—only to 'canceled' for administrative corrections.

Status indicating the refund request was canceled by the customer before processing. Marks the refund as canceled in the system.

This is initiated by the customer before the refund has been processed, typically during the 'pending' state. Once canceled, the refund process is halted and cannot be reinstated.

Business rule: This status can only be reached from 'pending' status, and once set, the refund request is effectively closed without further processing.

status.description:
Current processing status of the refund request in the refund management workflow. Follows a strict business transition path: 'pending' → either 'approved', 'rejected', or 'canceled'.

The status transitions are enforced to maintain workflow integrity, prevent invalid state changes, and preserve audit trail consistency. Business rules dictate that once a refund is 'rejected', it cannot be changed to 'approved', and 'canceled' refunds are only allowed from 'pending' state.

Changes to status are restricted to users with appropriate permissions and trigger automated email notifications to customers about the status update process.

amount.description:
Requested refund amount in the platform's base currency (USD) after validation. This value represents the exact monetary amount to be refunded to the customer.

The amount must be greater than 0.01 and less than or equal to the original order value. System validation enforces this rule before updates are accepted to prevent invalid refund amounts.

Business rule: For partial refunds, the amount must be a fraction of the original order value, but never exceed it. Currency precision is handled at the payment gateway level for final transaction processing.

reason.description:
Additional details or clarification provided by the customer regarding the refund request. Serves as communication channel between customer and platform for explaining the refund reason.

This field allows customers to provide specific information about the change in the refund request, such as 'Product arrived damaged' or 'Requested additional refund amount'.

Business rule: The field must not exceed 500 characters to maintain efficient customer support operations and data quality standards.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the payment method. Used as a reference for payment method configuration and integration.

This ID is always present in the database and will be used to identify this payment method across the application. It's system-generated and should never be provided by clients.

name.description:
Human-readable name for the payment method, such as 'Credit Card' or 'PayPal'. This name is displayed to end users during checkout.

Represents the brand or service name visible to customers making payments, helping them recognize the payment option they're using for transactions.

processorType.description:
The payment processor type used for this payment method, such as 'stripe' or 'paypal'. Determines how the payment is processed through the gateway.

This represents the technical platform or service handling the payment processing, such as Stripe, PayPal, or another payment gateway service.

supportedCurrencies.description:
List of currency codes supported by this payment method, in ISO 4217 format (e.g., 'USD', 'KRW'). Represents the currency types that can be used for transactions through this method.

These currencies define which currency types the payment method can process, allowing customers to choose appropriate currency options during checkout based on their location and preferences.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethod.ISummary.description:
Simplified view of payment method information for the shopping platform. This summary type is used in paginated lists and search results to provide essential payment method details without including detailed configuration.

Includes the payment method name, processor type, and supported currency codes to help users identify and select appropriate payment options during checkout. This is the standard format used in the shopping mall's payment method index API to enable efficient display of available payment options.

IShoppingMallPaymentTransaction.description:
Payment transaction entity representing a single payment record within the shopping mall ecosystem. This main entity type provides a complete view of payment details without sensitive payment card information or PCI-DSS sensitive data.

The PaymentTransaction entity captures all necessary information for payment processing, including amount, currency, status, gateway reference, and timestamps. It establishes a relationship with the order entity through the order field, enabling the platform to maintain payment-order associations.

This entity is used in responses for payment transaction details across customer, seller, and admin interfaces, always excluding sensitive payment details while maintaining compliance with financial regulations. It's the primary data structure for payment processing and reconciliation operations, serving as the single source of truth for payment status and details.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the payment transaction, generated automatically upon creation. Follows UUID v4 format for global uniqueness across all payment systems. Required for all transaction lookups and operations.

This field serves as the primary key for the payment transaction entity in the database and is used to reference transactions across different system components including orders, refunds, and payment methods. The identifier remains constant throughout the transaction lifecycle and is never modified.

In API responses, this field is required in the transaction details to enable precise retrieval and correlation with other payment-related data points such as order history and customer statements.

amount.description:
Monetary amount of the payment transaction in basic currency units. Always non-negative and represents the transaction value before any currency conversion.

The amount corresponds to the product/service value in the order that triggered the payment. This field is used for financial reconciliation and reporting purposes, and must match exactly the amount specified in the order details.

When processing payment status updates, this value is compared against the order's expected amount to identify discrepancies or fraud attempts.

currency.description:
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the payment amount. Must follow standard international currency code format.

Identifies the currency in which the transaction amount is denominated. This code enables proper currency conversion and financial reporting across multiple markets. It's fixed at the time of payment processing and cannot be changed after creation.

The code is validated against standard currency definitions and stored exactly as specified by the payment gateway to ensure financial accuracy and regulatory compliance.

oneOf.description:
Current payment processing status reflecting the transaction's lifecycle phase.

This status field tracks the transaction through its processing stages: from initiation ('pending'), to confirmation ('completed'), failure ('failed'), refund processing ('refunded'), or dispute ('chargeback'). Each status transition is logged for audit purposes.

The status value affects business logic such as order fulfillment, customer notifications, and settlement processing. It's critical for the user interface to correctly display payment status and provide appropriate user actions.

gateway_reference.description:
Reference ID provided by the payment gateway for this specific transaction. Acts as a key for payment gateway reconciliation.

This field contains the identifier used by the payment processor to uniquely identify this transaction within their system. It's required for contacting the gateway to resolve payment issues or retrieve detailed processing information.

The gateway reference is stored exactly as received from the payment processor and is used to connect transaction records to external payment processing records.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the payment transaction was first created. Records the initial payment processing initiation.

This field captures the exact moment the payment request was submitted to the payment gateway. It's used for time-based business rules such as payment deadlines and early settlement opportunities.

The value is generated automatically by the system at transaction creation and cannot be modified, serving as an immutable historical record.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the payment transaction status was last updated. Reflects the most recent activity on this transaction.

This field records the precise moment when the transaction status changed (e.g., from 'pending' to 'completed'), triggering business processes like order fulfillment. It's updated automatically on every status change.

This timestamp is critical for auditing purposes, to determine the timeline of payment processing, and for troubleshooting payment status inconsistencies.

code.description:
Unique business identifier for the order item. Generated as a unique code at order creation time to provide a human-readable reference for tracking within the order system.

The code is structured to be globally unique across all orders and follows the format: order-{orderCode}-item-{sequenceNumber}. It is used as the primary key for retrieving order items and is immutable after creation. The code remains constant throughout the item's lifecycle.

order.description: The associated order object. Reference to the parent order through the order business code (orderCode). This field uses .ISummary to provide complete order context without circular reference risks.

product.description: The associated product object. Reference to the parent product through the product business code (productCode). This field uses .ISummary to provide complete product context for shopping mall catalog display.

variant.description: The associated product variant object. Reference to the product variant through the variant business code (variantCode). This field uses .ISummary to provide complete variant context for product configuration.

quantity.description:
Number of units of the product variant being purchased. Represents the physical quantity ordered.

This field validates that the requested quantity is at least 1 unit. It's used for inventory calculations, order fulfillment, and billing, and automatically enforces business rules around minimum order quantities.

priceAtPurchase.description:
Price of the product variant at the time of purchase. Represents the price point that was confirmed at order placement.

This field stores the exact monetary value (in system currency) that was charged at this particular time, including any applicable discounts. Prices are non-negative and must be >= 0.

oneOf.description:
Current status of the order item reflecting its progress through the ordering and fulfillment process.

This status field tracks the lifecycle of the item from initial order placement (pending) through processing (processing), physical shipment (shipped), delivery confirmation (delivered), and any cancellation (cancelled). The status values are fixed and must match exactly one of the enum values listed in the schema.

The status is updated automatically during fulfillment operations and serves as the primary indicator of the item's current state for both customer visibility and internal order management.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when the order item was created in the database. Represents the exact time when the item was added to the order, matching the transaction timestamp.

This timestamp is automatically generated by the system when the order is placed and serves as a permanent record of when the item was added to the order. It is not modifiable and is used for audit trails and historical order analysis.

IShoppingMallOrderItem.description:
Detailed representation of an order item, including product details, ordering quantity, and transactional status. This schema reflects the data stored in the shopping_mall_order_items table and is used for displaying order item information to customers and sellers.

The schema implements an atomic operation design where all order item details are provided in a single response without requiring additional API calls for context. It includes all relevant attributes for viewing the order item within the system, with proper relationships to parent order, product, and variant entities through business code references.

The schema follows the security-first design principle by excluding any system-managed properties (like IDs) and by ensuring authentication context is handled via JWT rather than request body. All relation fields properly follow the object reference strategy (using code-based IDs and .ISummary references) for efficient data access.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the refund request, generated automatically and used for resource identification in the system.

This field is read-only and cannot be modified after creation. It should be stored as a UUID per database schema requirements and used as the primary key for refund request records.

requestDate.description:
Timestamp when the refund request was submitted, formatted in ISO 8601 standard.

This field provides a clear view of when the request was initiated and is used for ordering and searching historical requests.

The value is system-generated and cannot be changed by the user or application.

oneOf.description:
Current processing status of the refund request, which can be one of three values:

- 'pending': Refund request is awaiting processing
- 'approved': Refund has been approved and is being processed
- 'rejected': Refund request was denied by the system or administrator

This status field is updated through system automation and business rules to reflect the current state of the request.
