productId.description:
Product identifier linked to the inventory change.

This string value represents a globally unique identifier for the product in UUID format. It connects the inventory log entry to the specific product that was modified in the inventory system.

The UUID format ensures uniqueness across product lines and avoids collisions with other entities. Each product in the system has a unique identifier, and the inventory log ties back to this central product record.

The identifier is generated by the system upon product creation and never changes. Required for all inventory log operations involving products.

variantId.description:
Variant identifier for product-specific inventory changes.

This string value represents a globally unique identifier for a product variant in UUID format. It's used when the inventory change affects a specific variant of the product (like size, color, or style) rather than the product as a whole.

The variant identifier is optional as not all inventory operations require variant-specific tracking. When present, it provides precise location for the inventory change within the product variant hierarchy.

This field is primarily used for detailed inventory tracking at the variant level, allowing for more granular inventory management. The identifier is generated upon variant creation and remains immutable.

quantityDelta.description:
Change in inventory quantity.

This numeric value represents the amount by which inventory levels changed. Positive numbers indicate additions to inventory (e.g., receiving new stock), negative numbers indicate deductions from inventory (e.g., sales or returns).

The quantity delta is calculated as (new quantity - old quantity) at the time of the inventory change. It's always stored as a raw number without unit context, with units assumed to align with the product's standard unit of measure.

This field is critical for calculating the actual impact on inventory levels and for historical tracking of inventory changes across the system.

timestamp.description:
Timestamp when the inventory change was recorded.

This string value represents the exact moment the inventory log entry was created in ISO 8601 date-time format. It captures when the change occurred in the system, not when it was created.

The timestamp is automatically recorded by the system and cannot be modified. It's crucial for chronological ordering of inventory changes, auditing, and resolving timing discrepancies in inventory management.

This is the standard timestamp format used across the entire system to ensure consistency in time-based operations and reporting.

userId.description:
User who performed the inventory operation.

This is a reference to the user summary object for the individual who performed the inventory change. It provides essential context without exposing sensitive user information like passwords or session tokens.

The summary object includes the user's ID, name, role, and other non-sensitive information for audit purposes. It enables tracking of who made inventory changes without the need to fetch full user profiles for every log entry.

This field is critical for accountability and security audits, helping to track inventory modifications back to specific users in the system.

orderId.description:
Order identifier associated with the inventory change.

This string value represents a globally unique identifier for an order in UUID format. It's used when the inventory change is directly related to an order (e.g., deductions for sales, stock updates for order fulfillment).

The order identifier is optional as not all inventory changes are related to orders. When present, it provides a connection to the specific order that triggered the inventory change.

This field is important for tracking inventory changes across order processes and linking inventory to customer transactions in the system.

transactionId.description:
Payment transaction identifier related to the inventory change.

This string value represents a globally unique identifier for a payment transaction in UUID format. It connects the inventory change to a specific payment, typically used when inventory is adjusted due to payment processing.

The transaction identifier is optional as it only applies to inventory changes related to payment transactions. It allows linking inventory adjustments to specific payment events for accounting and reconciliation purposes.

This field is essential for financial reporting and reconciliation processes, helping to track how payment transactions impact inventory levels.

notes.description:
Additional comments or details about the inventory change.

This string value provides free-text explanation of the inventory change. It's optional but recommended for providing context beyond the basic operation details.

The notes field can include information about why the change was made, special considerations, references to internal processes, or any other relevant details not covered by other fields. It's particularly useful for complex inventory adjustments that require additional context.

Note: The string length is limited to 1024 characters to maintain database efficiency while still allowing sufficient detail.

IShoppingMallReview.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a shopping mall review optimized for list views. Contains minimal information necessary for display in product category listings and search results without exposing sensitive user information or internal system data. Includes essential review details to support customer decision-making while maintaining data privacy standards.

This schema is designed specifically for product review display in shopping interfaces where space is limited and performance is critical. The summary format excludes all non-essential fields such as review ID (not shown publicly) and avoids complex object structures that would slow down catalog displays. It prioritizes the most valuable customer-facing elements: the product context, reviewer identity, rating, and a condensed review excerpt.

Each field value is optimized for real-world shopping scenarios: the 0.5 increment rating scale reflects common e-commerce rating patterns, the 500-character content limit ensures reviews fit within typical UI containers, and the UUID identifiers guarantee unique references without being exposed to users.

The schema follows the business rule that only product and user summaries are exposed, not complete profiles, to maintain data security while still providing sufficient context for shoppers to evaluate reviews.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the review, generated upon creation following standard UUID v4 format. This value is immutable and used exclusively for internal system references - not exposed to users in interface displays. The UUID format ensures scalability across large review datasets while providing strong uniqueness guarantees to prevent collisions.

In the shopping context, this ID allows systems to track specific review interactions for analytics, moderation, and support requests without exposing user-facing information. It's the primary key used in database operations and API references for the review.

The system creates this ID automatically and never modifies it, ensuring consistent reference points for all review-related data across the platform, including associated product listings, user profiles, and administrative tools.

product.description:
Full product context for the review, displayed as a pre-filled summary without requiring additional API calls. This reference provides the minimal product information needed for context while optimizing performance.

The product summary includes key visibility elements like name, category, and image URL that customers need to identify the product being reviewed. It excludes detailed specifications that wouldn't contribute to the review context in list views, keeping data lightweight.

This design choice directly supports the business need to display relevant product information next to reviews without slowing down catalog loading times. The summary structure is designed to fit into standard interface components like product card grids and recommendation modules across mobile, tablet, and desktop platforms.

user.description:
User who wrote the review, displayed as a minimal profile summary that respects privacy while providing social proof. The customer summary includes only necessary visibility elements for review context.

This structure avoids exposing personal information like email addresses or full names while still showing the reviewer's public profile identifier. The summary format is specifically designed for review contexts where user identity needs to be partially visible but not fully exposed.

In the shopping context, this partial visibility encourages community interaction without compromising user privacy - reviewers can be recognized without revealing personal contact details, while customers can assess the credibility of reviews based on profile elements.

rating.description:
Customer's star rating on a scale of 1 to 5 with 0.5 increments representing overall satisfaction. This standardized rating format ensures consistency across all product reviews regardless of the reviewer's experience level.

The 0.5 increment allows for nuanced feedback while maintaining simplicity - customers can express intermediate satisfaction levels without overly complex rating systems. Most reviews cluster around 3.5-4.5, with the scale accommodating both positive and critical feedback in a unified format.

This rating field is the primary indicator for customers deciding whether to purchase a product, with higher ratings directly correlating to increased conversion rates across the shopping platform.

content.description:
Condensed review summary limited to 500 characters that captures the essence of the customer's experience. This is not the full review but a thoughtful excerpt that provides value in compact display formats.

The 500-character limit is carefully chosen to balance detail with performance - short enough to fit in standard UI elements like review cards, but long enough to include meaningful insights about the product. It excludes lengthy narratives and focuses on key benefits or drawbacks relevant to purchasing decisions.

This field appears in product detail pages, search results, and review filters, where space constraints require brevity while still providing contextual help for customers navigating shopping options.

created_at.description:
Timestamp of when the review was first submitted to the platform, following ISO 8601 format. This date is immutable and used for chronological display and filtering.

The creation timestamp helps customers immediately see the review's recency, which is a strong indicator of product quality (recent reviews may be more relevant). It's used in sorting review displays to show newest reviews first by default.

This field is critical for maintaining data integrity during review management operations - it never changes, providing a consistent anchor for all historical review operations and analytics.

IShoppingMallReviewComment.IRequest.description:
Pagination and filtering parameters used to control which review comments are retrieved from the system. These parameters are designed for efficient client-side consumption of paginated comment data, allowing customizable display and sorting of comments associated with a specific review.

The parameters support a range of common filtering and sorting patterns required for product review comment management. The system handles all pagination logic server-side, returning only the relevant page of results, which improves client-side performance and reduces network traffic for applications displaying extensive comment histories.

All parameters are optional with reasonable defaults, enabling the API to be used with minimal client configuration. The schema follows the standard REST API parameter convention for search filtering, ensuring compatibility and predictability for developers implementing client-side search interfaces. The properties have been carefully documented to match the business context described in the schema documentation.

page.description:
The page number of results to retrieve. Must be a positive integer greater than 0. For example, page=2 retrieves the second page of results when combined with limit=20, representing items 21-40. The default value (if not specified) is 1, which returns the first page of results.

This parameter is essential for paginated data retrieval patterns common in review systems. The value represents the requested page for the results to display, with 1-based indexing standard for most pagination implementations.

limit.description:
The number of review comments per page. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. If not provided, defaults to 20 to balance between data transfer and performance considerations. A limit of 0 would be invalid, as it would return no results.

This parameter determines the granularity of results returned to the client, affecting both network efficiency and user experience. The default value of 20 is commonly used in web applications to provide a balanced view without overwhelming the client with excessive data.

search.description:
Text search term to filter review comments by content. The server will perform a case-insensitive partial match on comment text. Should not contain special characters that could interfere with the search engine, though the service will attempt to handle common search patterns. The search parameters will be applied to the comment content field.

This parameter enables users to quickly find specific comments within a large collection. The implementation uses partial matching to provide a better user experience than exact matches, and it's case-insensitive to avoid user frustration with capitalization differences.

oneOf.description:
Field by which to sort the results. Valid fields are typically those that are indexed and commonly sorted on, such as 'created_at' for timestamp sorting, or 'rating' for comment quality ranking. The format must match the column name exactly, with underscores used for multi-word fields. This parameter is case-sensitive and must be one of the approved sort fields.

Sorting is critical for user experience in review systems where newer or higher-rated comments are typically displayed first. The approved sort fields ensure the system can optimize database queries with appropriate indexes to provide fast results.

Sorting is critical for user experience in review systems where newer or higher-rated comments are typically displayed first. The approved sort fields ensure the system can optimize database queries with appropriate indexes to provide fast results.

oneOf.description:
Sorting order direction. 'ASC' for ascending order (oldest first) and 'DESC' for descending order (newest first). Only applicable when sort_by is specified. If sort_by is provided but order is absent, the default is 'DESC' to ensure new comments appear first where common practice dictates.

This parameter works in conjunction with sort_by to determine both the criteria and direction for data ordering. The default of DESC is standard in most modern applications where users expect the most recent results to appear first.

content.description: Comment content in markdown format validated against platform business rules. Must not contain prohibited or offensive content as defined in business rules.

IShoppingMallReviewComment.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new review comment on a product. The comment content must be in markdown format and undergoes validation against platform business rules to prevent prohibited or offensive content. This DTO is used in the POST /shoppingMall/customer/reviews/{reviewCode}/comments operation where 'reviewCode' is a path parameter identifying the target review.

The comment author is automatically determined from the authenticated customer session, so no author information is required in the request body. The system validates content for prohibited material and enforces markdown formatting to maintain platform consistency. Comments are subject to moderation before becoming visible in the product review interface.

Business rules specify that comment content must comply with the platform's content policies as detailed in Security & Compliance documents. The validation process ensures adherence to the defined guidelines, including restrictions on offensive language and spam content.

IShoppingMallOrderCancellation.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new order cancellation. This represents a customer's request to cancel an order that is in a cancellable state. The request includes the reason for cancellation and optional details.

Business context: Cancellation requests are initiated by customers who want to cancel orders that are still in 'pending' or 'processing' status within 24 hours of purchase. These requests are subject to automated validation to ensure they meet the business rules before being processed.

Field explanation: The reason field is mandatory and must contain a customer-provided explanation. The cancellationReasonCode is optional and maps to predefined system categories. Notes provide additional context for order processing staff.

reason.description:
The reason provided by the customer for cancellation. This is the mandatory field that explains why the customer wants to cancel the order.

Business requirement: This field must be a valid, non-empty string describing the reason for cancellation. It helps the system track cancellation patterns and improve customer experience based on feedback.

Validation rules: Must be at least 1 character in length. Empty strings are not allowed.

IShoppingMallProductSpec.description:
Product specification entity that contains technical details required for variant-specific product information displayed to customers on the shopping platform. This entity represents details such as color options, size specifications, material composition, and other attributes that impact the product variant selection experience.

The specification entity is directly linked to the parent product (via the 'product' object reference), which allows for dynamic filtering of specifications based on product catalog placement. This relationship ensures that as products are updated or restructured within the catalog, their associated specifications automatically reflect contextual changes.

Created and managed solely by sellers (using their authorized access tokens), these specifications are publicly accessible to customers across all product detail pages. The specifications are designed as non-sensitive data that supports transparent shopping decision-making, and they're integrated with the product catalog system to provide immediate consistency between listing and detailed specifications.

This entity uses additional metadata fields ('created_at', 'updated_at') to facilitate change tracking and ensure orderliness in specification management on the platform. The specification 'id' field provides a universally unique identifier for database operations and API references, while 'spec_code' ensures uniqueness within a specific product's specification set.

id.description: Universally unique identifier generated using UUID version 4 standards. This identifier serves as the primary key for the specification record in the database and is used across all API references and internal database relationships. It remains immutable once assigned, ensuring stable references for history tracking and audit trails.

product.description: Object reference linking the specification to its parent product entity. This reference is a full IShoppingMallProduct.ISummary object, providing access to essential product properties like name, category, price, and image_url for contextual display. The relationship is strictly one-to-many (one product can have multiple specifications), and is validated against the shopping_mall_products table for data integrity.

spec_code.description: Business identifier for the specification within the context of its product, rendering it unique only for that specific product (not globally unique). Used as an identifier in API endpoints and navigation to avoid unnecessary joins with the product catalog. Follows the pattern {product_code}_{sequence_number} to ensure uniqueness for product-level specifications.

color.description: Color attribute identifier for the product variant, providing the precise color in product display. Does not contain hex codes or RGB values; instead, uses common descriptive terms for customer clarity (e.g., 'red', 'navy blue', 'light green'). This color tag is crucial in filtering specifications by color when browsing deviant products.

size.description: Size attribute for the product variant, containing specific dimensional specifications and how the size is represented (e.g., 'EU 42', 'S-M-L', '20cm x 15cm'). This fields standardizes size description across all products and uses retailer-specified size formats to facilitate customer comparison and filtering by size.

material.description: Identity of the material composition for the product variant, specified in terms commonly understood by consumers (e.g., '100% cotton', 'aluminum alloy', 'polyester blend'). This enforcement ensures customers can make purchasing decisions based on material composition, which is critical for product quality perception and fit in the market.

description.description: Comprehensive technical description of the product variant, including all relevant specifications, material composition, and detailed attributes visible to customers on product pages. This communication-oriented description is formatted for customer understanding, using no technical jargon, and is a key factor in conversion rates on the shopping platform.

created_at.description: UTC timestamp indicating when the product specification was created, automatically set by the system during insertion. This timestamp is not allowed to be modified by users and is critical for historical tracking, audit logs, and customer understanding of the relevance of specifications (e.g., newer specifications may have up-to-date details).

updated_at.description: UTC timestamp of the last modification to the product specification, automatically updated by the system on every change. This field is critical for version control of specifications and helps ensure customers see the most relevant technical data, especially in cases where attributes are frequently updated based on seller input.

order_id.description:
Identifies the specific order that is being paid for. This is a required reference to an existing order in the system.

The value must be a valid UUID format that matches an order ID in the orders system. The UI or mobile app will provide this value when confirming the payment flow.

amount.description:
The monetary value of the transaction being processed. This must match the amount specified in the order for the payment to be validated.

This field should be a positive numeric value with up to two decimal places for precision. It represents the exact amount in currency units required for the payment transaction.

gateway_reference.description:
A unique identifier provided by the payment gateway for this specific transaction. This is essential for reconciliation with the payment gateway's system.

The value must be stored exactly as received from the payment gateway without any modifications or additions. It is provided by the gateway's response to the payment request.

oneOf.description:
Represents the current status of the payment transaction as recorded from the payment gateway.

The value must be one of: 'pending', 'completed', 'failed', 'refunded'. These correspond to transaction states in the payment processing workflow.

currency.description:
Specifies the currency used for this transaction, following ISO 4217 standards.

This must be a lower-case currency code (e.g., 'usd', 'krw', 'jpy') that matches the currency of the order that is being paid.

IShoppingMallPaymentTransaction.ICreate.description: Request DTO for creating a new payment transaction record for a customer's order. This DTO contains only the necessary fields to set up a payment transaction without including sensitive payment data. The operation requires the user to be authenticated with a valid session, and the user ID must match the order's owner. Added mandatory session context fields (href, referrer) for self-authentication.

IShoppingMallReviewVote.IUpdate.description:
Schema for updating an existing review vote. This DTO represents the modifiable properties of a review vote record in the system, allowing for partial updates to vote rating without requiring full entity retransmission. Used as the request body for the 'update vote status on a product review' endpoint (PUT /shoppingMall/customer/reviews/{reviewCode}/votes/{voteCode}).

The schema excludes identity fields (reviewCode, voteCode) as these are already provided in the path parameters. It also excludes authentication-related fields as these are automatically populated from the authenticated customer context via the JWT authorization token. Vote type cannot be changed after creation, so it's not included in the update schema.

rating.description: The numerical rating value of the review vote. Represents the score given to the product review, typically on a scale from 1 (lowest) to 5 (highest) representing the product's quality or helpfulness. Should be a non-negative number with no more than 3 decimal places in most cases. This field is updated when customers modify their vote ratings on product reviews.

IShoppingMallRefundRequest.IRequest.description: Filtering and pagination parameters for refund request collection. This request DTO implements comprehensive search capabilities for customer refund requests, supporting status filtering, date range filtering, payment method filtering, and product category filtering. The properties include essential pagination controls, filtering parameters that match the database schema, and sorting options that optimize performance for large refund request datasets. Pagination parameters (page, limit) are required as they directly enable the server to handle multiple pages of results efficiently. These are standard requirements for the API operation which serves a paginated response as described in its documentation.

oneOf.description: Filter refund requests by current status. Only requests matching this status will be included in the results. The status field refers to the current lifecycle state of the refund request. Valid values include 'pending' (request is undergoing review), 'approved' (refund processing has started), and 'rejected' (request has been declined). The API enforces these exact status values, using the database's status field directly.

page.description:
Page number for pagination. Starts from 1. This is required for all paginated requests to avoid returning all results at once.

Minimum valid page number is 1. Values less than 1 will be rejected by the server. This parameter is essential for implementing pagination in the API to handle large data sets efficiently.

Page number must be a positive integer. The API interprets values less than 1 as invalid requests and returns an HTTP 400 error response.

limit.description:
Number of items to return per page. Default is 20, with maximum allowed value of 100 to prevent excessive data loading on single requests.

The limit parameter determines how many refund records will appear per page. Values above 100 are not allowed to ensure reasonable API payload sizes. This parameter helps optimize network efficiency and server handling of requests.

A limit of 0 would be invalid and the API would reject it. The minimum value of 1 prevents empty response pages.

status.description:
Status filter for refund requests. Allows filtering by one or multiple refund statuses to identify requests matching specific business stages.

Valid status values include 'pending', 'approved', and 'rejected'. Using an array enables filtering for multiple statuses simultaneously. If not provided, all statuses will be returned. This flexibility supports common administrative workflows where users need to view multiple status categories at once.

The API automatically validates status values against business rules and rejects invalid values. Status filters are applied to the OrderRefund table through direct database references, eliminating the need for complex joins in the backend implementation.

minAmount.description:
Minimum refund amount to include in results. Amounts must be numeric and non-negative to include in positive financial filtering.

Amounts below 0.01 are invalid and will be rejected by the server. This parameter is mutually exclusive with maxAmount; it specifies the lower bound for the amount range. The minimum amount of $0.01 aligns with standard currency denominations and prevents fractional amounts from appearing in financial calculations.

All amounts are processed as decimal values with two decimal places, reflecting standard currency handling throughout the system.

maxAmount.description:
Maximum refund amount to include in results. Amounts must be numeric and non-negative to include in positive financial filtering.

Amounts below 0.01 are invalid and will be rejected by the server. This parameter is mutually exclusive with minAmount; it specifies the upper bound for the amount range. The maximum amount supports the full range of typical refund values up to $999,999.99.

When both minAmount and maxAmount are provided, the API returns only refunds within that specific financial range, providing precise filtering for financial reporting and analysis.

minDate.description:
Earliest date for processing date range. Must be in ISO 8601 format (e.g., "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z").

The processing date refers to when the refund request was created. This parameter allows filtering requests by date range to find recently processed refunds or historical data. Valid dates must be formatted according to ISO 8601 standards to ensure consistent date parsing across the system.

When minDate is specified without maxDate, the API returns all refunds created on or after the specified date. The date range filtering is applied directly at the database layer for optimal performance.

maxDate.description:
Latest date for processing date range. Must be in ISO 8601 format (e.g., "2024-12-31T23:59:59Z").

The processing date refers to when the refund request was created. This parameter allows filtering requests within a specific time window, working with minDate to define the full date range. The API validates date formats strictly to maintain data integrity across all operations.

When both minDate and maxDate are provided, the system returns refunds with creation dates falling strictly within the specified range. Time zone conversion is handled automatically, with all dates stored in UTC format.

oneOf.description:
Field to sort results by. Valid values are applicationDate, amount, or status.

The default sort order is applicationDate in descending order, which shows most recent refunds first. Changing this allows views sorted by the most economic (by amount) or by the most common status. The applicationDate field represents the timestamp when the refund was created, the most natural sorting metric for time-ordered data.

When sorting by amount, the API calculates values directly from the financial data without additional operations, ensuring consistent sorting performance across large datasets.

The 'amount' field represents the processed refund amount after any applicable processing fees have been subtracted, making it a reliable metric for financial analysis.

sortBy.description:

The default sort order is applicationDate in descending order, which shows most recent refunds first. Changing this allows views sorted by the most economic (by amount) or by the most common status. Sorting by applicationDate is the standard for chronological data, while amount and status sorting serve specific analytical purposes.

The system automatically handles sorting direction, though the direction parameter is required to specify ascending or descending order.

oneOf.description:
Sort direction. Ascending (asc) or descending (desc).

Default direction is 'desc' for all fields. 'asc' provides ascending order views, which can be useful for looking at oldest entries or lowest amounts first. The direction parameter determines the order of results in the response.

When sorting by applicationDate in ascending order, the API returns refunds starting from the earliest date, which is helpful for historical analysis or identifying long-standing refunds. This behavior is consistent across all sort fields.

Default direction is 'desc' for all fields. 'asc' provides ascending order views, which can be useful for looking at oldest entries or lowest amounts first. The direction parameter determines the order of results in the response.

Descending order is the default, providing a 'most recent first' view. This is the standard presentation for most time-sensitive data like refund requests, enhancing the user experience by showing the latest activity first.

direction.description:
Sort direction. Ascending (asc) or descending (desc).

Default direction is 'desc' for all fields. 'asc' provides ascending order views, which can be useful for looking at oldest entries or lowest amounts first. The direction parameter works in conjunction with the sortBy parameter to determine the final order of results.

The API validates direction values strictly to maintain consistent sorting behavior across all endpoints. 'desc' is the default, though the client can explicitly specify 'asc' for specific use cases.

IShoppingMallOrderRefund.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for refund filtering.

This DTO contains all parameters required to filter and paginate refund requests based on search criteria including refund status, amount ranges, and processing date ranges. It supports sorting for improved user experience and query optimization. The implementation provides flexible filtering capabilities without requiring complex joins.

Customers and administrators can use these parameters to view refund information associated with specific orders through the GET /orders/{orderCode}/refunds endpoint. All filters are applied to the OrderRefund table, which maintains direct references to the order through the order_id field.

Pagination parameters are designed to prevent excessive data loading on single requests. Page numbers start from 1, and limit values are capped at 100 to ensure reasonable API payload sizes. The system rejects invalid values such as negative numbers for amounts and page numbers below 1.

The refund status filter allows for both single and multiple status criteria using string or array values. This flexible approach supports common business workflows such as filtering for 'pending' and 'approved' statuses in a single request.

Sorting enables optimization of user experience by allowing display of most recent refunds first (applicationDate), followed by amount or status sorting. Default sorting behavior returns results in descending order by application date.

IShoppingMallProductCategory.ISummary.description:
Product category summary representation used in paginated lists and embeds for shopping mall category listings. Represents minimal category information required for display in product browsing interfaces, including basic attributes and essential relationship references for category hierarchy navigation.

This summary type includes all necessary fields for category list views while excluding detailed composition relationships (like product lists) to optimize performance. The category hierarchy relationship uses .ISummary format to prevent circular references and maintain API efficiency.

The schema follows the atomic operation principle for read operations, ensuring consumers can display complete category information from a single API response without additional requests. Parent category references are included as summaries for hierarchy context, while detailed category data remains in the full entity type. All timestamps are validated against the database schema to ensure they exist for this entity.

id.description: Unique identifier for the category. Must be a valid UUID format string to match database column constraints. Used as the primary key for category identification and URL references in category-related endpoints. This identifier is system-generated and immutable once created.

name.description: Category display name used in product browsing interfaces. Must be 1-100 characters long for usability and consistency across platform UI/UX. The name should reflect the actual product category meaning without technical terms or internal codes. Used as the primary label for category selection and display in category navigation.

description.description: Detailed description of the category purpose and scope. Used to provide context for search and filtering, particularly in multi-level category structures. The maximum length of 1000 characters ensures it's detailed but doesn't overwhelm the UI. This field is used exclusively in search functionality and detailed category views, not in basic list views.

parent.description: Parent category reference for hierarchical organization. Provides context in the category tree structure without full child lists. The reference uses .ISummary pattern to maintain consistency with atomic operation principles, preventing circular references and ensuring hierarchical information is immediately available with a single API call. This relationship is directional (child points to parent) and follows the BELONGS-TO rule for reference types. This field is optional for root categories. It can be null in the database for root categories.

is_active.description: Category visibility status in product catalog. Determines whether the category is publicly visible and available for product listing. When true, category is included in standard product browsing flows; when false, category is hidden from most users but may remain accessible to administrators. This status is managed by platform administrators.

created_at.description: Timestamp of category creation in ISO 8601 format, including timezone offset. Represents the exact date and time when the category was first added to the system. Used for sorting category listings chronologically and in analytics. This field exists in the database and is automatically handled by the platform.

IShoppingMallProductVariant.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a product variant optimized for display in order, inventory, and inventory adjustment contexts. Includes only essential fields necessary for referencing product variants without data bloat. This summary form contains id, name, and SKU information for quick identification during inventory management and order processing operations. Used as references in order items, low stock alerts, and inventory adjustments.

The schema follows security-first principles by excluding all system-managed fields while maintaining complete business context. It's designed to provide the minimal necessary information for efficient listing in paginated responses without requiring additional API calls for context.

This type is optimized for performance in list views, ensuring small payloads while keeping all business-critical information. The schema's structure matches exactly what's referenced in IShoppingMallLowStockAlert, IShoppingMallInventoryAdjustment, and IShoppingMallOrderItem schemas to maintain relationship consistency across the API.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the product variant instance. Represents the primary key in the product specifications table and is used for referencing specific variant records across the system. Must follow standard UUID format for uniqueness and security against guessing attacks.

This field is never provided by the client but is generated by the system upon product version creation. It serves as the stable identifier for the variant, enabling consistent tracking throughout order and inventory management processes.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the product variant. Includes distinctive features such as color, size, or other variant-specific information (e.g., 'Red, 128GB', 'Medium, Black').

The name is visible to users in product listings and inventory management interfaces. It's designed to help customers quickly identify variant differences and to enable efficient inventory categorization without requiring full product details.

sku.description:
Stock Keeping Unit code for the variant. Uniquely identifies the specific variant in inventory tracking systems, used for tracking inventory levels across warehouses.

The SKU follows the business's standardized naming convention, enabling accurate inventory management and cross-referencing with external systems. It's a critical identifier used throughout the fulfillment process, from order placement to inventory updates.

IShoppingMallProductCategory.IRequest.description:
Search criteria, filters, and pagination parameters for product categories.

This request allows for comprehensive filtering of product categories through multiple criteria including partial name matches, hierarchical structure, category status, and creation date. The parameters enable precise search and sorting functionality for catalog management operations.

The system provides flexibility for administrators and sellers to search through category hierarchy and retrieve categories based on active status. It supports sorting by name, category hierarchy, creation date, and active status in either ascending or descending order.

Pagination parameters allow for efficient data loading, with defaults set to return 10 categories per page starting from the first page. This design optimizes performance for browsing large category datasets while maintaining user-friendly defaults.

search.description:
Partial match text used to search for category names. Enables fuzzy matching that is insensitive to case and space, allowing users to quickly find categories by partial name without needing exact spelling.

The search functionality supports multiple search patterns including substring matching, and can handle categories with complex naming conventions. This field is optional as it enables basic searches without filters.

Example usage: "electronics", "phone", "wireless" would match categories like "Electronics", "Mobile Phones", "Wireless Accessories".

The parameter provides flexibility in how categories are presented in the user interface. Category name sorting follows alphabetical order, hierarchy follows the order in the category tree structure, creation date uses ISO 8601 timestamp format, and status sorts by active/inactive state.

When unspecified, defaults to sorting by category name for the most user-friendly experience.

The default of 'asc' ensures consistent behavior for users unfamiliar with sorting options, reducing potential confusion in category listing.

This parameter allows administrators to manage content visibility without deleting categories. Inactive categories can be reactivated without losing historical data. The status filter enables precise access to only the categories that need to be managed or displayed.

The status parameter is particularly useful for maintaining a clean catalog interface while preserving historical category structures.

This parameter enables navigation of category trees and allows for viewing categories at specific hierarchy levels. It supports filtering for top-level categories (root), main categories (parent), and subcategories (child).

The hierarchy filter works specifically with the category tree structure, making it useful for managing product catalogs with multi-level hierarchy organization.

page.description:
Page number in pagination. Specifies which page of results to return, starting from 1 for the first page.

The parameter supports sequential navigation through large category datasets, enabling efficient browsing of categories in manageable chunks. The page number must be a positive integer, defaulting to 1 if not specified.

For applications with many categories, page navigation is essential for performance and user experience, as loading all categories at once would be inefficient and confusing for users.

limit.description:
Number of results per page. Specifies how many categories should be returned per paginated response, with a minimum of 1 and maximum of 100 to prevent performance issues.

The limit parameter controls the granularity of data loading, balancing between performance and user experience. A default limit of 10 is commonly used to keep pages readable while not overwhelming users with too much data.

The maximum limit of 100 is set for performance reasons, ensuring the system doesn't suffer from excessive memory usage during large data transfers.
